column1: A blockchain-based credibility evaluation scheme for navigational event dissemination in the internet of ships
column2: This paper proposes a blockchain-based credibility evaluation for navigational event dissemination, which constitutes a significant functionality for the ship trust management over Internet of Ships (IoS). This enables evaluating and calculating the credibility of the navigational events announced by other ships during their navigation. The presented scheme verifies the credibility of navigational events by introducing cooperative ratings from the involved ships. Bayesian inference models are utilized as the basic estimation about the authenticity of the event, upon which the Hidden Markov Model (HMM) is leveraged to update the reputation of the relevant ships from their current reputation and the ratings they comment about the event. In addition, a Delegated Proof of Stake (DPoS) consensus mechanism based on the reputation of the ship, called R-DPoS, is designed to prioritize ships with higher trustworthiness values to be elected as witness ships, to maintain the stability and efficiency of block generation in the system. In order to validate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed scheme, a series of simulation experiments are conducted. The experimental results show that the proposed scheme has an accuracy of more than 80 % for navigational events in most cases, which not only effectively recognize the credibility of navigational events and update the trustworthiness value of the relevant ships, but also suppress the malicious cyber behavior of ships, enhancing the security and stability of the cyberspace of the IoS.
column3: 8 Conclusion In this paper, we propose a blockchain-based credibility evaluation for navigational event dissemination towards vessel trust management scheme over the Internet of Ship. This scheme allows ships to collaborate in verifying the authenticity of navigational events through cooperative commenting. By doing so, it contributes to the maintenance of a generally trustworthy cyberspace within the IoS. Additionally, in order to address the possibility of malicious behavior by ships, the proposed scheme implements a comprehensive reward and punishment mechanism for ship trustworthiness values. This mechanism serves to discourage and penalize malicious ships, while incentivizing honest ships to comply with the established rules and maintain their trustworthiness value. Furthermore, the introduction of the R-DPoS consensus mechanism plays a pivotal role in enabling candidate witness ships with high trustworthiness values to more readily secure the position of witness ships, thereby enhancing and strengthening the overall trustworthy cyberspace within the IoS. The simulation results presented in this paper demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed scheme for trust management in a distributed cyberspace, particularly within the context of the IoS.

column1: Exploring the physical-digital interface in blockchain applications: Insights from the luxury watch industry
column2: Counterfeit products are an increasing issue across the luxury sector. Blockchain applications exhibit the potential to mitigate counterfeit risks and facilitate the growing secondary markets by enabling product authentication and digital proof of ownership. In this study, we adopt a qualitative multiple-case study design and conduct interviews with informants from four blockchain projects in the Swiss luxury watch industry. We identify the industry-specific drivers and barriers to blockchain adoption and specifically explore the challenges at the physical–digital interface. Beyond an in-depth description of the problems, our findings suggest two main data management hurdles related to the validity of input data and data synchronicity. The main challenge, however, is to establish an unequivocal link between the physical watch to its digital record on the blockchain. We present several invasive and non-invasive linking approaches and discuss their potential advantages and disadvantages. Further, we outline different areas for future research. Overall, our study addresses a timely issue of blockchain applications, contributing to the operations and supply chain management literature and supporting blockchain use case design in practice.
column3: 6 Limitations and conclusions Unlike any other industry, luxury goods are plagued by counterfeits. In this paper, we empirically explore major blockchain projects that aim to address this issue and provide product identification and proof of ownership. We outline the Swiss luxury watch industry’s motivation and barriers to adopting blockchain. We also specifically emphasize the challenges associated with the physical–digital interface and discuss potential linking approaches. While our study provides important implications for academia and practice, it is not without limitations that need to be considered. First, our qualitative data is largely cross-sectional. Consequently, we are unable to assess the longitudinal dynamics of the blockchain projects in our sample. Second, we discuss the advantages and disadvantages of different invasive and non-invasive linking approaches based on the sample firms’ considerations and publicly available information regarding the approaches. However, implementing these approaches at our sample firms was either planned or in very early stages, and thus, the practical experience and insights are limited. We encourage future studies to gather more data on the implementation and utilization of different linking approaches to further gain insights into the challenges at the physical–digital interface. Third, our setting is the Swiss luxury watch industry. While we provide substantial reasons for this choice and argue for the generalizability of our findings to the luxury sector, we believe that the physical–digital link and its challenges need to be examined in various settings. Despite these limitations, by studying a practically relevant phenomenon, we make a timely contribution to the operations and supply chain management literature. We strongly believe that an in-depth exploration of one of blockchain’s greatest adoption barriers – the challenges associated with linking the physical object and the digital records – can support practitioners in the design and development of adequate use cases, ultimately realizing the technology’s operational and financial value.

column1: FUSION-Fog Computing and Blockchain for Trusted Industrial Internet of Things
column2: The industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) is currently foreseen as a foundation to implement the Industry 4.0 vision. However, device heterogeneity and the need of integration and configuration exposes the industrial infrastructure to potential threats, such as black-hole, man-in-the-middle, and malicious configuration attacks. In this article, we investigate how to manage distributed trust information and to enable trusted configuration actions in the IIoT, by opportunistically intermingling blockchain with the software defined networking and container orchestration technologies. In particular, we focus on how the joint and coordinated adoption of such technologies can make technicians’ interventions on industrial equipment both easier and more trusted. To this purpose, we present the design of a software architecture to simplify the management, configuration, and assessment of IIoT systems, and we discuss our experiences with the application of the proposed architecture in a railways use case.
column3: In this article, we presented FUSION, a software platform born with the aim to show the advantages to combine the blockchain with SDN and container-based orchestration for the trusted management of devices in the IIoT. The platform was centered around the notion of FESNs as computing nodes for trusted IIoTs that can be flexibly reconfigured to act as end devices (L0FESN) or fog/edge nodes (L1FESN). We envisioned the use of the blockchain to both manage the trust information, in a federated way, and to securely manage FESN management in terms of reconfiguration. The presented railways business case has shown how the platform can simplify and make more trusted the intervention of technicians on equipment connected to edge devices, even when those technicians do not trust one another. This is also coupled with continuous assessment, which can be used to plan preventive maintenance, on the basis of tradeoffs between costs (e.g., how often to repair) and reliability, also taking into account possible changes that can happen during the life of the system. Again, monitoring information, collected by the trusted nodes of the system, is securely stored by FESNs using the blockchain.

column1: Risk assessment of maritime container shipping blockchain-integrated systems: An analysis of multi-event scenarios
column2: Blockchain applications in maritime logistics services face uncertainties and risks, obstructing a broader and more sustainable adoption. Although the operational risk of blockchain-integrated systems (BISs) is significant, studies in this area are still conceptual and scarce. This research is a mixed-methods risk analysis focusing on (1) modeling the risk situation by a connected network of potential disruptive events in container shipping BISs, and (2) applying a quantitative risk analysis with probabilistic indexes considering the multiplicity of multi-event risk scenarios (MESs). Thirty-two telephone interviews with experts from container terminal operators, shipping companies, and freight forwarders helped establish a risk network with the description of 25 vertices and 54 directed connections. The quantitative analysis of 64 web survey responses provided insights and foresight about different characteristics of each risk and causal connection. The results enable a comprehensive view of the potential failure modes of blockchain applications. This study is the first to explore the potential risk situation in container shipping BISs with inputs from the industry. The applied methodological framework expands the toolkit of risk researchers, analysts, and managers against the fast-paced development of digitalization in maritime logistics and supply chain operations.
column3: 6 Conclusion The increasingly large scale and complicated structure of the information flow emphasize the importance of sustainable technology adoption. This study conducted an exploratory mixed-methods research to analyze operational risks in container shipping BISs. Interviews with industry experts strengthened and provided industry-specific contexts for the risk identification results. Risks and causal connections were identified to establish a risk network, modeling and visualizing BISs’ complex risk situations. A quantitative analysis was employed to untangle the risk situation from multiple aspects, utilizing the availability of probabilistic inputs and the concept of MESs to interpret the established risk network. This paper has two primary contributions to maritime logistics risk management literature. First, it established a risk network supported by a comprehensive knowledge base from blockchain academic literature (provided by Nguyen et al. (2020) ) and industry-specific context provided by experts. The findings contribute to the discussion of risk and uncertainty as a barrier to blockchain adoption and digitalization sustainability. The risk network indicates the importance of the collaboration between the shipping industry and the blockchain research community for sustainable digitalization and the CSO-ICT cooperation in the risk management efforts of BISs. The qualitative analysis result suggests multiple factors nurturing operational risks, including container shipping and maritime logistics’ underdevelopment and unreadiness in terms of digitalization and standardization, and friction between industry’s trust-based business model and blockchain’s decentralized and transparent economic model. Second, this study is the first to provide a probabilistic quantitative analysis of container shipping operational risks with the presence of BISs, providing insights and foresight into the DEs’ potentials of these systems. The results indicate that IORs might be less frequent in BISs, but they contain possibilities of pervasive and accumulated consequences. The result indicates the current applications’ limited contribution to data security, contrasting to data availability, data utilization, procedure simplification. This vulnerability threatens data integrity and confidentiality under various significant MESs, suggesting that cybersecurity development and practices are vital in the IOR prevention/mitigation plans of CSSPs. The low assurance of data quality also constrains the applicability of smart contracts, which is the backbone of most BISs’ desired features. To the risk analysis of container shipping operations, this study proposed RNA as a novel framework to analyze complex risk situations from multiple aspects with probabilistic indexes. The framework enables the optimization of risk management efforts considering MESs. The framework is recommended for both practitioners and researchers in related risk management activities, including assessing and monitoring risk levels, risk prevention, and mitigation planning. The risk-proof extent of proposed blockchain applications can also be examined by customizing the risk network under the specific settings, helping the adopters in BIS solution evaluation, audit, and maintenance. The RNA framework supports mixed-method risk analysis and encourages a more prudent view into expert-based risk studies (i.e., uncertainty indexes), which are essential yet scarce in logistics and supply chain digitalization. As an exploratory study, this study proposes five areas that require further investigations and research. First, there are other key parties involved in container shipping BIS that this study did not cover. Including the viewpoints of shippers, banks and authorities would shed more light on the intentions of adopting the emerging technology. Second, apart from a risk-focus approach, exploring the challenges and recommended adaptive strategies to each group of CSSPs in adopting BISs can offer a more comprehensive view of blockchain’s applicability in the industry. In this topic, the blockchain vision of the nation-state, the industry, and the companies play a key role in directing the implementation efforts. Third, this study has not yet provided a detailed analysis of the magnitude of the risks themselves. A prudent approach would be combining the individual and multi-event approaches to study the magnitude of MESs’ accumulated consequences. A risk index scale for MESs could be established, enabling other network analysis techniques to be applied (e.g., clustering, optimization). Fourth, more specific risk analyses focusing on a risk (e.g., cybersecurity) or group of risk (e.g., related to smart contract), a specific system, and a particular risk bearer are required to provide more details for action-ready risk mitigation/prevention planning. Fifth, the proposed analysis framework could be applicable to other risk situations in supply chain and digitalized systems. However, such generality is still unproven and need further dedicated empirical studies.

column1: Blockchain and network governance: learning from applications in the supply chain sector
column2: Abstract Blockchain applications have the potential to greatly improve operational efficiency and effectiveness along the supply chain. Although we know what the barriers to the adoption of blockchain are, we know little about how firms overcome these barriers to reap the benefits of the technology. A particular challenge in adopting blockchain applications is the need to build and implement them among a network of users, requiring firms to collaborate. To manage and advance such collaborative efforts, blockchain projects install a centralised leadership. There is thus a tension between the need for centralised leadership and decentralised control to justify the use of blockchain technology. In this study, we investigate how blockchain projects navigate this tension. We employ a multiple case study methodology to compare five collaborative blockchain applications that are live today. Our findings indicate that the case applications all combine centralised management with decentralised oversight in a similar manner. We argue that this combination of centralised and decentralised control is a great benefit for the successful development and implementation of blockchain applications. The results underline that to benefit from blockchain technology in supply chain applications, an important collaborative organisational effort is necessary.
column3: This study shows that developing and implementing blockchain applications in a supply chain context is associated with an important organisational effort. In the five case applications we investigated, it is this organisational aspect of collaboratively building blockchain applications that stands out with regard to its complexity and resource intensity. Jointly organising the implementation of a technology among a group of firms has been difficult in the past and will be difficult in the future. Blockchain technology is no exception. Despite all the buzz around blockchain as a novel and potentially disruptive technology, the requirement to involve many stakeholders in building blockchain applications makes it a difficult technology to implement.

column1: BACS: blockchain and AutoML-based technology for efficient credit scoring classification
column2: Credit evaluation is of high scientific significance and practical use, especially in today’s plight of the world suffering from the COVID-19 epidemic. However, due to the difficulties inherent in credit scoring model building which involves a large number of data mining steps and requires a lot of time to process the data and build the model, efficient and accurate credit scoring methods are are urgently required. Aiming to solve this problem, we propose BACS, an blockchain and automated machine learning based classification model using credit dataset so that the credit modelling processes are performed in the pipeline in an automated manner to eventually obtain the classification results of credit scoring. BACS scheme consists of credit data storage to blockchain, feature extraction, feature selection, modelling algorithm and hyperparameter optimization, and model evaluation. Firstly, we propose a mechanism for credit data management and storage using blockchain to ensure that the entire credit scoring system is traceable and that the information of each scoring candidate is securely, efficiently and tamper-proofly stored on the blockchain nodes. Next, we design a pipeline using a random forest model to effectively integrate the key steps of credit data feature extraction, feature selection, credit model construction, and model evaluation. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed automated machine learning-based credit scoring classification scheme BACS can assess the credit condition efficiently and accurately.
column3:
As an essential component of the credit system, the evolution of credit scoring systems plays a key role in the progress of the overall credit scoring system. With the rapid progress and popularity of big data technology, credit scoring based on big data has received widespread attention and has generated a series of credit scoring applications based on big data and machine learning. In particular, the economic downturn and credit crisis caused by the global COVID-19 epidemic has also heightened the urgent need for an efficient and stable credit scoring system. The aim of this paper is to develop a automated credit scoring classification model that reliably and quickly differentiate the credit status of credit assessors. Therefore, we propose BACS method for efficient credit scoring, including credit feature extraction, feature selection, regression model construction and model hyperparameter optimization. Experimental results demonstrate the efficient and accurate credit scoring classification performance of our BACS scheme.

Although a multitude of credit scoring methods have made some progress in the field of big data credit scoring, the data utilized in current credit scoring research is still only a fraction of big data, and many data sources, especially social data scattered in cyberspace, have not been fully utilized. How to facilitate the sharing and exchange of credit data among agencies will be an essential part of our future research. In addition, for future research we will consider optimizing the efficiency of blockchain data storage in BACS system, such as the methods utilized in Yang et al. (2021); Qi et al. (2020), to guarantee the privacy security of disparate data sources while storing credit data securely. Moreover, we will adopt credit model building mechanisms such as neural architecture search technology (Mellor et al. 2021; Yan et al. 2020) to enhance the performance and efficiency of classification models in the BACS scheme.

column1: Who should invest in blockchain technology under different pricing models in supply chains?
column2: In recent years, members of supply chain have rushed to invest in blockchain technology to improve product traceability for more profits in their operations. When both the manufacturer and retailer can afford the cost of blockchain, a question arises: who should invest in blockchain technology? To benefit from blockchain investment, the retailer such as Walmart, which has a higher power in the choice of pricing models than the manufacturer, will examine the blockchain investment motives of supply chain members and carefully design the pricing model: a wholesale pricing model or an agency pricing model. In this paper, we establish game-theoretic models to explore the interaction between the retailer's choice of the pricing model and supply chain members' choice of the blockchain investor. Our results show that a bit surprisingly, the demand of privacy-sensitive customers decreases even if they do not use blockchain traceability services provided by supply chain members. We also obtain the retailer's equilibrium pricing model choice together with the supply chain members' blockchain investment decisions, which depends on the commission rate. An interesting insight is that when the commission rate is medium, supply chain members will be locked in a prisoner's dilemma where both the manufacturer and retailer want to free ride on the blockchain investment to maximize their own profits, which ultimately leads to the loss of both parties due to no blockchain investment. Finally, we design a cost-sharing contract under the Nash negotiation framework when the two parties face conflict in the choice of blockchain investor.
column3: 7 Conclusion In the supply chain consisting of a manufacturer and a retailer, where the retailer has the power to choose a pricing model, both the manufacturer and retailer have the ability to invest in blockchain. We analyze in this paper the interaction between the retailer's choice of pricing model and supply chain members' choices of blockchain investor, showing the impacts of this interaction. The core conclusions and insights are as follows. (i) There exists a tension between the total demand and demand of privacy-sensitive customers when adopting blockchain technology. Although using blockchain will increase the total demand, it will reduce the demand of privacy-sensitive customers, which applies to both the wholesale and agency pricing models. The reason is that privacy-sensitive customers do not use blockchain traceability services for privacy concerns, but the adoption of blockchain technology has increased the product's retail price. The above conclusion is a warning to enterprises that the adoption of blockchain technology is likely to harm privacy-sensitive customers. In order to retain privacy-sensitive customers, enterprises should take measures (e.g., by promising that customer information obtained will not be used for other purposes and making efforts to protect it) to make such customers feel that their privacy is protected. (ii) The choice of supply chain members for “optimal blockchain investor” under different pricing models is identified. The manufacturer's investment in blockchain technology is always preferred by supply chain members under the wholesale pricing model. However, under the agency pricing model, the optimal choice depends on the commission rate. For the manufacturer and retailer, the manufacturer should invest by itself rather than be a free rider if the commission rate is small; otherwise, the retailer investing in blockchain is their best choice. The above conclusions reveal that free-riding behavior in blockchain investments can lead to a win-win situation for both the manufacturer and retailer under certain conditions. Consequently, in order to benefit from blockchain investments, supply chain members should be aware that free-riding behavior in blockchain investments may be positive, and voluntarily bear the cost of blockchain investments. (iii) The retailer's optimal pricing model choice and the supply chain members' optimal blockchain investment decisions would mainly depend on the commission rate. If the commission rate is polarized (i.e., small enough or large enough), the retailer should choose the wholesale pricing model, where the manufacturer should invest in the blockchain. For example, Nestle Coffee uses the wholesale pricing model to sell its products on JD.com, and it should invest in blockchain technology by itself to enable consumers to trace its product information if the commission rate is polarized. If the commission rate is moderate, the agency pricing model is the optimal choice for the retailer. When the agency pricing model is determined, the manufacturers' investment is preferred by the supply chain members if the commission rate is relatively small, which is consistent with the practice that Moutai uses the agency pricing model to sell products in Tmall Mart and establishes its own blockchain anti-counterfeiting and traceability system. However, if the commission rate is relatively large, they prefer the retailer to invest. For example, Wyeth sells its milk powder on JD.com through the agency pricing model and JD is responsible for investing in the blockchain. Note that the manufacturer and retailer could have misaligned incentives in the region where the commission rate is medium: they both want to let its partner make investments and become free riders. The above conclusions provide clear guidance to supply chain members on how to choose appropriate pricing models and blockchain investors to maximize profits for both parties as well as avoid falling into the prisoner's dilemma. (iv) Cost-sharing contract under the Nash bargaining framework may be an effective way to resolve the supply chain members' conflict in the choice of blockchain investor. Specifically, in the conflicting area, the manufacturer and retailer should jointly invest in blockchain technology and share part of the investment costs according to their bargaining power, respectively. After using the cost-sharing contract, the profits of the manufacturer and retailer are higher than that when they are in conflict, resulting in a win-win situation. The cost-sharing contract in this paper provides an effective solution for supply chain members caught in a prisoner's dilemma of blockchain investment in practice. To show the robustness of the findings, we consider the following three extensions: (a) the manufacturer bears the additional operating cost to label the product; (b) blockchain investment decisions are made before the retailer's choice of pricing model; and (c) the manufacturer and retailer have asymmetric blockchain investment cost coefficients. These extensions confirm the robustness of our main models. There are some limitations of our study, which provide directions for our future work. For example, we only consider the situation that the supply chain contains only one manufacturer and one retailer. In reality, there should be more manufacturers and retailers, as well as other supply chain members such as upstream suppliers that need to be considered. It would be interesting to study the choice of blockchain investor where a manufacturer sells a product through multiple competing retailers.

column1: Blockchain-enabled electric vehicle orderly charging optimization
column2: Abstract The increasing prevalence of electric vehicles (EVs) urges charging station operators (CSOs) to expand their networks. However, currently CSOs operate independent EV charging service platforms separately, which poses inconvenience for EV users and hinders the efficient utilization of charging infrastructure. This paper introduces a consortium blockchain-enabled EV charging service platform (CB-EVCSP), which leverages novel orderly charging guidance models (OCGMs) encoded as smart contracts to integrate and coordinate the efforts of CSOs. The CB-EVCSP not only mitigates trust and security concerns but also enhances the utilization of charging facilities. Both multinomial logit (MNL) and mixed MNL models are developed to characterize the interaction between charging station recommendations and EV users’ choice behaviors, where a coefficient of variation based fairness criterion is used to ensure distribution fairness. We provide equivalent reformulations and design efficient constraint generation algorithms. Numerical experiments are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed models and algorithms.
column3:
To provide a trustworthy and efficient charging service, this paper develops a framework of CB-EVCSP with an MNL-based OCGM based smart contract. To characterize EV users’ heterogeneous charging preferences, an MMNL-based OCGM is further proposed. Based on the equivalent tractable MISOCP reformulations of MNL-based OCGM and MMNL-based OCGM, an efficient constraint generation algorithm is developed by tackling the non-linear fairness constraints with gradually generated gradient-based cuts.

The proposed CB-EVCSP can address the trust and security challenges of the recommendations and transaction processes because of the shareability, transparency and tamper-resistance of blockchain. Moreover, the numerical experiments show that the CB-EVCSP can improve the CSOs’ revenue and distribution fairness. It motivates the CSOs to join the platform. However, a higher fairness criterion level can reduce total revenue of the CSOs. In practice, the CSOs and the CB-EVCSP should determine the level of fairness criterion to make a trade-off between the revenue and distribution fairness. The results of sensitivity analysis also suggest that it is sufficient to provide EV users reasonable number of recommendations, and the CSOs should provide similar and competitive charging prices at the CSs located closely to improve the revenue and ensure the distribution fairness.

CB-EVCSP also provides opportunities to conduct other businesses. For instance, CB-EVCSP can provide the charging appointment system to improve the schedule effectiveness among the CSOs. In practice, the charging demands have an unbalanced spatial-temporal distribution. Utilizing the charging appointment system, the CB-EVCSP can apply the dynamic pricing method to guide and incentivize the users to charge the EV in the CSs with idle piles or to charge during the leisure time. Moreover, considering the CSs of renewable energy generation, the CB-EVCSP can also provide a trustworthy vehicle-to-grid service to balance the grid and smoothly integrate renewable energy.

column1: Investigating Healthcare 4.0 Transition Through a Knowledge Management Perspective
column2: The impact of technological innovation on the healthcare sector is becoming increasingly significant, and the number of studies exploring this topic is rising rapidly. However, studies on the digital transition of healthcare services are still a challenge, both from a theoretical and managerial perspective. In this context, knowledge management discipline can guide the evolving environment to cover this research gap. Indeed, the digital transition is transforming how healthcare professionals access data, handle information, and manage knowledge by adopting 4.0 enabling technologies. Thus, drawing on the SECI model, this study aims to investigate the healthcare sector's technological innovation through a knowledge management perspective, and evaluate the impact of 4.0 technologies on knowledge creation processes (i.e., socialization, externalization, combination, internalization) in the healthcare domain. Finally, the article investigates the critical areas of the digital transition, and the future research directions that remain to be addressed.
column3: This article provides a transparent picture of the different 4.0 enabling technologies supporting the four phases of the SECI model in healthcare. Notably, by reviewing the existing literature on the digital transition of healthcare in terms of knowledge management processes, we have developed a structuring framework. The present SLR provides different theoretical contributions. First, it provides a framework highlighting the role of digital transition and knowledge creation processes while specifying whether tacit and explicit knowledge is being managed in healthcare. Accordingly, these results can emphasize what the literature has looked at and which enabling technologies have gained much attention. Notably, the proposed taxonomy shows that the majority of 4.0 enabling technologies support the phases of socialization and internalization, thus allowing physicians to learn more quickly about patients' state of health and consequently formulate faster and more accurate diagnoses. Indeed, it is feasible to use wearable technologies to self-diagnose and then transfer the results to physicians, promoting the exchange of tacit knowledge between healthcare professionals and patients. Furthermore, our synthesis provides prescriptive considerations concerning future research avenues' development according to the proposed research framework. Specifically, the papers' content analysis has highlighted four primary areas of investigation concerning the support of enabling technologies to knowledge socialization; knowledge externalization; knowledge combination; and knowledge internalization. From these four areas of investigation, some gaps in the literature have emerged. In providing a comprehensive overview of what scholars have studied so far on the digital transformation in healthcare through the lens of knowledge management, this article highlighted the enabling role of cloud technologies in every phase of the SECI model [110], [184], [185], [186]. Their application was emphasized in many contexts and functions, highlighting their pervasiveness and potential. Due to rapid population growth, the complexity of researching and analyzing the massive amount of patient data worldwide is growing. This aspect allows for improved data-based decision-making and faster development of precision medicine. A productive research frame has begun in recent years around the IoT role, especially in explaining data acquisition. Some authors showed how the IoT solutions, connecting things, sensors, and other smart technologies, allow companies to collect valuable data to improve healthcare, e.g., [73], [187]. Furthermore, many articles deal with training for medical and nursing students that can take place through technologies such as augmented reality and simulation, e.g., [157], [161], [163]. Thanks to these technologies, they can first put new knowledge into practice by simulating real situations and using the knowledge acquired. Applying the principles and tools for knowledge management will provide the basis for improving health decisions [188]. Using technologies to exchange knowledge between physicians, nurses, or patients can improve clinical practice and health management. Progress in information and collaboration in healthcare, support for informed decisions, EHR systems, practical communities, and advanced care planning are several transformative healthcare opportunities [189]. Another research gap concerns the low number of articles for horizontal and vertical integration technology in healthcare. Vertical integration concerns the organization's communication and sharing of knowledge, while horizontal integration concerns parties external to the organization, such as suppliers or external consultants. The few articles are synonymous with a low focus on communication and knowledge sharing analysis. These integration systems are designed to transform the way workers interact with each other and with the environment, improving both end-users' and service providers' experience. Besides the focus on specific technologies, overall, the analyzed studies are qualitative. This, in turn, calls for research that seeks to examine organizational learning phenomena in the digital era through quantitative approaches (e.g., larger scale quantitative studies). Furthermore, future studies should adopt a longitudinal perspective of analysis. The digital transition takes time to be implemented, and healthcare organizations also require adjusting to this transformation. This means that the implementation stage and differences within the same organization exist as the digital transition takes its course, eventually affecting the intertwined effects between implementing digital technologies and organizational learning over time. This article provides practical contributions. Healthcare professionals could use this study's findings to acquire knowledge regarding the use of different 4.0 technologies that could support day-to-day operations, enabling better data-driven decision-making. Digital technologies, such as IoT, cloud computing, and blockchain, are becoming more popular in the healthcare industry to gather and analyze data and transmit data between operators and patients. For instance, blockchain technology offers the possibility to provide a secure and reliable system for managing and exchanging EHRs data. Interoperability across systems allows for the elimination of local health [190], [191], allowing for the exchange of clinical data over long distances, resulting in improved healthcare for people and reducing geographic obstacles to data analysis and interpretation. This study also suggests that healthcare organizations should invest in digital learning tools (e.g., virtual reality, smart glasses) to improve employee learning and satisfaction, patient quality of care, and overall performance. As for the research limitations, our analysis was carried out using only the Scopus database. Second, although the filtering process may have excluded relevant research, our systematic review's rigorous procedure has decreased the risk that the study omitted would have provided details that would dramatically alter our findings. Despite these limitations, we first contribute to the literature on the digital transition of healthcare using a knowledge creation perspective. Finally, we offer future research opportunities for those desiring to focus on this field. We hope that this structure will converge innovation study resources in healthcare research and practice. Primary data should be acquired from sizeable, highly innovative healthcare organizations experienced in relying on technological innovation processes to achieve this aim. More in detail, interviews with organizational members should be conducted to understand the degree of implementation of enabling technologies and how it has affected healthcare organizations' modus operandi, especially regarding the socialization, externalization, combination, and internalization processes, thus helping scholars to assess the influence of digitalization on knowledge creation. Then, in-depth case studies should be carried out for specific technological innovation projects to scrutinize how enabling technologies are now being employed to manage knowledge and the main constraints and advantages of projects not involving digital solutions. Besides further case studies should be carried out for different developed country in order to highlight similarities and differences linked to the different country environment.

column1: Inter-organisational collaboration through blockchain governance and smart contracts: a design science research approach
column2: This study investigates how blockchain and smart contracts provide governance for inter-organisational collaboration, focussing on Virtual Enterprises and Virtual Breeding Environments (VBEs) as manifestations of collaborative networks. We employ a Design Science Research (DSR) approach to design and evaluate a conceptual framework as our artefact. Guided by Enterprise Modelling (EM) methodology, we first propose the blockchain governance mechanisms of on-chain voting, token-based reputation, privacy-preserving data sharing, and identity management, which align with organisational requirements and behavioural aspects of collaborative networks. Second, we empirically validate, test, and provide a simulation analysis of the blockchain mechanisms. The findings represent preliminary evidence of the conceptual framework's generalised utility, highlighting the need for further empirical investigation into blockchain's relation with contractual and relational governance in inter-organisational settings. This study contributes to theory by advancing the understanding of inter-organisational collaboration through blockchain governance in the operations management field. We also offer practical insights to guide the design and action towards blockchain-enabled governance systems.
column3: Governance is an important unit of analysis for organisational competitive advantage and engagement in collaborative value creation. Blockchain has emerged as a technological infrastructure for enterprise applications that differs from other solutions due to its ability to enforce agreements between several parties, providing a digital form of governance. For this purpose, this study addresses a literature gap in understanding how blockchain can provide effective governance for collaborative networks. Using a DSR approach, we designed and evaluated a conceptual framework for inter-organisational collaboration through blockchain governance and generated new theoretical and managerial insights to advance knowledge. 7.1. Theoretical contributions This study contributes to the literature by introducing a conceptual framework that, despite referring to Virtual Enterprises and VBEs as manifestations of collaborative networks, addresses a common issue in operations management: governance. Therefore, it contributes to the knowledge of developing a blockchain solution that addresses a class of problems in practice. The proposed blockchain governance mechanisms were identified through EM, formalised in research hypotheses, and tested analytically via statistics and simulations, which provided preliminary results about their generalised utility and long-term feasibility. Our DSR approach offers theoretical insights into how those mechanisms address inter-organisational collaboration governance requirements (which answers the research question) and how blockchain may be adopted in this context. We extend researchers' understanding of inter-organisational collaboration through blockchain governance, contributing to research aimed at developing technological rules directly applied in practice and adding to the ongoing debate on blockchain's relation with traditional contractual and relational mechanisms. 7.2. Practical contributions Our DSR approach offers managers and transacting parties insights for viewing, designing, implementing, and operating effective blockchain governance mechanisms. The 4EM method comprises practical guidelines for delivering a blockchain-based governance system closely aligned with organisational requirements and behavioural aspects of collaborative networks. Through this approach, managers can use their experience appropriately to create governance structures according to the application, contributing to the success of inter-organisational relationships and the attainment of positive network-level outcomes. The governance mechanisms can be operationalised and tested as part of the design principles of proofs-of-concept and prototype tests in relevant practical environments, advancing knowledge regarding operating and maintaining blockchain-enabled organisations. 7.3. Research limitations and future research The primary limitation of this study is its sample size. While we focussed on experts' opinions and employed complementary analysis (statistical and simulation-based) to address this limitation, results should be interpreted as preliminary, considering the different perspectives in blockchain governance and operations management. Future research should test our proposed mechanisms with in-depth and larger empirical evidence. Despite this limitation, this study provides a valuable foundation for further investigation in this emerging field. Though demonstrating the utility of the proposed framework, the blockchain governance mechanisms in our research are delimited to our scope and unit of analysis. Future investigations can leverage the DSR approach to assess whether the proposed mechanisms are generalised to other scenarios. For instance, power imbalance in decision-making may be desirable in supply chain networks or VBEs where organisations are highly hierarchically structured (e.g. due to the nature of the industry sector or the central position of an organisation in the value chain). Researchers may investigate whether an on-chain voting system linked to the reputation system is applicable, with the lead organisation having greater voting power in decision-making. Furthermore, the hierarchical structure between organisations would emphasise the role of identity management and privacy policies based on entities' different rights and responsibilities.

column1: Collaborative Governance: Blockchain-Based Federated Learning for Construction Safety Service
column2: Deep learning (DL) models are increasingly used to identify unsafe activities for the construction safety service (CSS). However, two typical issues threaten DL training process performance: poor security and privacy in data sharing. To address these problems, a blockchain-based federated learning (BCFL) framework is proposed from a collaborative governance perspective to obtain optimistic DL models for CSS. Two special works of this BCFL framework are that 1) it develops the federated learning empowered privacy-preserving data sharing with the principle of sharing data model weights instead of raw data (especially for one DL application for CSS, the Fed-YOLOv4 model for workers’ unsafe behavior identification task is developed) and 2) it explores two blockchain-based secure model sharing strategies that involve blockchain–interplanetary file system combination and model training contribution computing. Then, the smart contracts are further developed with the strategies above to streamline the workflow of federated DL model training. Finally, we apply the proposed framework to the practical subway project. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can improve the DL model training and acquire global DL models for CSS with good accuracy. Our findings indicate that great data security and privacy ensured by introducing blockchain and federated learning can optimize data sharing and then DL models can be improved. Moreover, this study provides managers with a collaborative governance perspective on how DL models can be improved and further applied to CSS. This enables managers to quickly understand project safety performance and make timely managerial decisions for construction management.
column3:
DL models are increasingly used to identify unsafe activities for CSM. However, in construction safety practices, DL has broad applications but this too often functions at the risk of infringing security and privacy in data sharing. Our study aims to address the following question: How to solve security and privacy concerns in construction safety data sharing for exploiting the true potential of AI (deep learning models)?

To fill this knowledge gap, this study contributes to the literature by highlighting the impact of data security and privacy on DL applications from the collaborative governance perspective. This study also proposes a novel BCFL framework to obtain security and privacy-preserving data sharing for collaborative DL applications in CSS. Two special works of this BCFL framework are as follows. 1) It develops the FL-empowered privacy-preserving data sharing with the principle of sharing data model weights instead of raw data. Especially for one DL application for CSS, the Fed-YOLOv4 model for workers’ unsafe behavior identification task has been developed. This provides practitioners a collaborative governance perspective on how DL models can be improved and further applied for CSS. 2) It explores two BC-based secure model sharing strategies and further integrated into SC designed to streamline the workflow of federated DL models trained in a BC network. Especially, 1) blockchain-IPFS-based FL node management and model storage scheme and 2) MTC-based aggregator selection and reward mechanism are proposed to provide a secure sharing environment and further streamline FL model sharing.

From the theoretical and practical perspectives, the contributions of this study are twofold.

Developing a novel security and privacy-preserving data-sharing approach from a collaborative governance perspective for the CSS.

The ability to generate GDLMs for CSS with good accuracy.

column1: Pre-positioning supplies with blockchain-supported inventory sharing in relief supply chains
column2: Addressing the management of pre-positioning relief supplies, this paper proposes an innovative joint government-enterprise model that integrates shared inventory with additional enterprise production capacity reserves. The study analyzes scenarios with and without blockchain technology to identify optimal conditions for pre-positioning shared supplies and production reserves. The results indicate that, in most cases, an increase in the optimal inventory quantity corresponds to a decrease in the enterprise’s production capacity reserve. In high-disaster-probability scenarios, enterprises maintain smaller production capacity reserves. Regardless of whether blockchain technology is utilised, under certain conditions, increases in supply and cost parameters can enhance enterprise profits. Supply-specific and cost parameters play a crucial role in influencing decision-making. Furthermore, this paper evaluates the conditional benefits of blockchain technology, which demonstrates contrasting effects on optimal reserve quantities and production capacity reserves in numerical analysis. This research advances shared inventory models by emphasizing production capacity reserves and exploring the application of blockchain technology in this critical domain.
column3: This paper investigates the optimisation of emergency relief supplies within a shared inventory model jointly managed by governments and enterprises. It introduces a shared inventory contract model and evaluates two scenarios: one integrating blockchain technology and one without. The study derives optimal decision-making conditions and analyzes the impact of various parameters on profit and cost outcomes in both scenarios. The shared inventory model and optimal decision-making strategies proposed in this paper aim to assist governments and enterprises in better pre-positioning critical relief supplies, minimising waste from storage costs or supply expiration, and enabling a faster and more efficient response to disasters. Joint reserves between governments and enterprises alleviate resource pressures during emergencies, making the approach highly applicable to real-world emergency management, particularly in resource-constrained environments and complex supply chains. For instance, in the ‘7.20’ Henan rainstorm disaster, the study illustrates how blockchain technology and the proposed shared inventory strategies can enhance supply reserve efficiency and improve disaster response outcomes. 6.1. Implications The practical implications derived from the numerical results offer valuable guidance for decision-makers in managing relief supply chains. Firstly, the results highlight that as the probability of disasters increases, governments should allocate more resources to pre-positioned inventory, while enterprises can reduce their production capacity reserves due to the increased reliability of shared inventory. This suggests that in high-risk areas, prioritising government-controlled stockpiles is essential for ensuring a faster and more effective disaster response. Furthermore, the integration of blockchain technology into shared inventory systems enhances transparency, mitigates the risk of fraud, and provides real-time tracking of supplies. This not only improves accountability but also strengthens trust between governments and enterprises, a critical factor for effective coordination during crises. Blockchain technology reduces the risks of improper supply management and material loss, enabling enterprises to achieve long-term cost savings through more efficient operations. The study also reveals that market price fluctuations significantly influence the optimal inventory levels and production capacity reserves of enterprises. Higher prices incentivize companies to increase their inventory reserves, thereby stabilising supply availability in emergencies. For governments, lower prices may reduce the need for large pre-positioned reserves; however, careful monitoring of market trends is crucial to prevent inventory shortages during disasters. 6.2. Conclusion and limitations This paper explores the application of blockchain technology in emergency relief supply chains, demonstrating its significant impact on optimal pre-positioning quantities in shared inventory models. The findings show that, under specific conditions, both governments and enterprises are inclined to adopt blockchain technology, highlighting its potential to enhance supply chain management in emergency relief scenarios. These results offer a theoretical basis for managing emergency relief supply inventories and open new possibilities for blockchain applications in this field. While this paper advances the understanding of shared inventory models and emergency relief material reserves, it has several limitations. First, the analysis focuses on reserves managed by governments and enterprises, without considering broader supply chain factors such as multiple suppliers or contributions from social organisations, which are critical in real-world disaster response. Expanding the scope to include these elements would provide a more comprehensive perspective. Second, this study adopts a single-period model, which does not reflect how reserves may degrade or lose efficiency over time. Future research could investigate multi-period models to better capture the evolving nature of emergency supplies and their long-term management. In conclusion, addressing these limitations in future research will help develop a more comprehensive and practical framework for managing emergency relief supplies. column1: Blockchain Technology for Embracing Healthcare 4.0
column2: Nowadays, health data are fragmented and scattered across various systems and technologies. Complex support infrastructures, data system silos, and administrative bureaucracy have led to inefficiencies and inefficacies. This article aims to propose a blockchain platform to share big health data in real time between the authorized actors while ensuring a high level of health information protection. The proposed platform can offer a highly innovative approach to administering benefits and keeping all parties in sync. Implementing a blockchain for managing health data is a valuable support for diagnosing and monitoring the progress of the therapies of individual patients under treatment. In addition, it helps to reduce the time required for the exchange of information and keep the healthcare operations under control. Healthcare organizations and ecosystems will benefit from having a complete picture of a patient's health condition and reaching a global audience through the blockchain platform.
column3: This section concludes the study by highlighting its theoretical and practical contributions and identifying different future research directions. A. Practical Contributions This article has provided a blockchain infrastructure for future healthcare organizations and ecosystems. Whereas typically, a patient to gain access to their medical records would need to apply to their health service provider and pay all associated administrative fees to have these released to them, with the proposed blockchain platform, the user would provide consent to have their data retrieved on their behalf and stored free of charge. Once this has been carried out, the patient would then use the blockchain platform to have a standardized, single point of access to those records at their discretion, also eliminating the need for additional administration fees. Utilizing the teleconsultation platform, users can have dramatically decreased waiting times and costs associated with travel. Therefore, in addition to patients, the blockchain-based platform designed is expected to benefit several stakeholders. Clinicians using the blockchain platform would have immediate access to conduct teleconsultations. This aspect will provide an additional revenue stream, meaning they could practice without any overheads other than a computer with an internet connection. This availability would decrease the chance of cancellations due to patients being unable to attend a consultation physically. Cutting this variable out saves on facility expenses, administration costs, and the need for additional staff. Patients should have control over their health records, and they should also benefit from the potential value they possess. Users will be given clear information about how their data are being used and what data will be required. In many cases, anonymized data will be permissible, ensuring the privacy of everyone involved. Healthcare professionals will benefit from having a complete picture of a patient's health condition. A single accurate record will be the sole place providers need to look for patient data, provide peace of mind, and reduce time spent on gathering records. Moreover, providers would benefit from not constantly investing in upgrading or upkeeping their health record systems. As a result, the proposed approach maximizes interoperability across the various healthcare organizations. After contacting the patient to obtain permission to access the data, the physician creates the report on the platform and shares it with all the healthcare professionals involved. Therefore, after getting consent, any physician of any hospital will be able to view the whole history of the patient's visits and reports. Furthermore, the blockchain platform can connect research institutions with users willing to have their health data used in studies in a health data marketplace. Researchers would have the ability to reach a global audience of patients through the blockchain platform. This would increase the potential sample size used in research and improve the accuracy of the results. Costs would be reduced by pulling the relevant information from a participant's health record with its consent. Pharmaceutical and research companies will also benefit from the changes brought in by our platform. They will seek out patients who have opted to be contacted by researchers so that these institutions can interact directly with the patient. Companies will no longer need to approach a hospital or clinic and go straight to the people whose information will be used. This aspect will increase efficiency, but it is a more transparent process that strikes a symbiotic and sustainable relationship in the entire healthcare ecosystem. Therefore, the advantages of using our blockchain platform concern 1) patient data security, privacy, and confidentiality as well as 2) cost savings, 3) virtual connectivity between various hospitals and research organizations, and 4) overall better quality of care thanks to patient monitoring, traceability of health records, and telemedicine services. B. Theoretical Contributions Regarding the theoretical perspective, this study contributes to the literature on the design of healthcare platforms by providing a holistic blockchain architecture to improve EHR interoperability and telemedicine services. Notably, blockchain technology was used to guarantee access to patients' medical histories without violating their privacy. With the use of this revolutionary platform, the information will be included in a shared database that healthcare professionals may access while protecting patient privacy and reducing IT risks. Furthermore, the theoretical perspective in applying the DSRM to an IT artifact is compelling, given that the proposed blockchain platform describes healthcare ecosystem behaviors, has a clear perceived usefulness, and affects both single actors and ecosystem organizations [71]. This perspective, confirming the multifaceted nature of the digital transformation process, suggests an insight into the role of blockchain in the dynamics of cooperation among the various categories of actors, as well as exploring its implications in the establishment of an efficient and effective EHR ecosystem. In the meantime, it has allowed identifying a contribution in terms of new bases in research about the disclosure of intangible value by contributing to a major comprehension of the principle of the “internet of values” [81], [82]. C. Future Research Directions The future investigation includes the potential for creating dynamic, intelligent contracts employing artificial intelligence to address cross-domain diversities [70]. In addition, future studies could conduct surveys with different healthcare professionals to accurately assess the platform's usefulness, accuracy, and effectiveness. Finally, future research includes investigating how blockchain affects organizational procedures in healthcare facilities and carrying out focus groups with patients, physicians, and developers to fully comprehend the advantages and potential drawbacks of the adoption of technology in the healthcare sector.

column1: A new model for production and distribution planning based on data envelopment analysis with respect to traffic congestion, Blockchain technology and uncertain conditions
column2: The production and distribution planning problem, where incomplete information from the manufacturer factories is available to the distributor, is prevalent in the real world. Yet, researchers have not focused sufficiently on this field of research. Therefore, our paper offers a two-level multi-objective optimization of production and distribution planning for the two-stage supply chain based on the Data Envelopment Analysis method, which minimizes both the cost and the traffic congestion caused by the establishment of distributor warehouses. In addition, transparency through the blockchain technology and uncertain conditions through stochastic and fuzzy programming are considered in the supply chain design. The proposed model is first transformed by using Karush–Kuhn–Tucker into single-level linear programming and then solved by fuzzy goal programming. Next, the obtained solutions are measured and sorted in terms of efficiency. In this regard, the solutions are categorized in terms of cost-based strategies, traffic congestion, demand satisfaction, and optimality. For the purpose of enabling comprehensive supply chain management, the solutions are aggregated according to various strategies and the results show that two solutions are the most efficient, one focusing on cost and the other focusing on traffic congestion.
column3:
In this paper, the two-stage supply chain has been investigated in a way that the distributor plays the role of the leader and the manufacturer plays the role of the follower, where the leader has access to incomplete information about the manufacturing companies. In this regard, the inputs and outputs of the factories are collectively visible by the leader. To this end, a two-level multi-objective optimization model for the production and distribution planning problem is proposed in which the manufacturer’s behavior from the distributor’s viewpoint is formulated based on DEA. This paper incorporates innovative factors such as transparency, traffic congestion, demand-driven operations, and uncertain conditions into the proposed optimization model. This paper investigated transparency through the blockchain technology based on connections among supply chain members, traffic congestion due to the degree of saturation created by established warehouses of the supply chain, demand-driven operation based on reverse flow and reworking, and uncertainty through stochastic programming and fuzzy programming. The two-level model is first converted into a linear single-level model by the KKT condition and then solved by fuzzy goal programming. The results are evaluated by an efficiency sorting strategy according to the criteria derived from the objective functions, optimality, and demand satisfaction. By solving the numerical example, we found that demand plays a prominent role in the supply chain. In addition, strategies based on the leader cost, follower cost, traffic congestion, optimality, and demand satisfaction were introduced for supply chain managers. On the other hand, in order to have more comprehensive management in the supply chain, various strategies were aggregated and efficient solutions were identified so that one of the two efficient solutions focused on traffic congestion and the other focused on cost. One of the limitations of this research is access to data, because DEA models need real data for evaluation. In contrast, our research provides many research opportunities for researchers in light of the problems we introduced in relation to DEA-based production and distribution planning, traffic congestion, transparency, and uncertainty. As for theoretical development, we suggest that researchers consider sustainability, vehicle types, multi-period models, and other uncertainty conditions and DEA models in their future research. The model presented in this paper can be used in other case studies and the analysis derived from the strategies presented in this paper can be offered to supply chain managers.
