column1: Generative heuristics-driven for blockchain-enhanced reputation systems and dynamic optimization in short food supply chains
column2: Recently, short food supply chains (SFSCs) through online platform are proposed as alternatives to overcome issues of traditional supply chains. The objective is to deal with fluctuating demand, freshness constraints, and trust issues. Online platforms use reviews of customers to manage the supplier–customer matching. However, such reputation system remains vulnerable to manipulation. To address this issue, blockchain technology (BT) is proposed. This article deals with the dynamic online matching in SFSCs using BT. First, the problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP). Then, a rolling horizon (RH) is proposed as a baseline method. A deep reinforcement learning (RL) hyperheuristics (DRLH), where generative artificial intelligence (AI) (GenAI) is used to draw the local search operators, is used to improve the solution quality. Extensive experiments are conducted on real-world SFSCs scenarios. Findings reveal that blockchain-based reputation system enhances the customer satisfaction, reduces contract failures, and increase platform gains.Keywords: Short food supply chainsblockchaingenerative AIdeep reinforcement learningheuristicsoperational Research
column3: This study explored the integration of blockchain-based reputation systems and GenAI-driven optimisation to enhance supplier–consumer matching in SFSCs. Unlike traditional approaches that focus solely on aligning supply and demand, the proposed platform leverages blockchain to enforce trust through smart contracts and immutable feedback, while GenAI generates adaptive heuristics to support dynamic decision-making in uncertain environments.We addressed two main research questions. Our findings show that blockchain-based reputation mechanisms significantly improve customer satisfaction, supplier accountability, and platform profitability. Smart contracts encode commitments transparently and automatically update reputations, building trust, and reducing transaction risks. We analysed the influence of key contextual variables, such as demand volatility, transparency, freshness, and organic level, on platform outcomes. The extended sensitivity analysis reveals clear trade-offs between trust assurance and operational inclusivity, showing how stricter quality thresholds can increase satisfaction but reduce match rates and gains.Despite its contributions, the framework faces some limitations. Its success depends on the level of digital adoption and regulatory support in different SFSC contexts. GenAI requires access to quality data, which may be limited during the early phases of platform development. Moreover, our results are based on simulations, and real-world deployment is necessary to confirm the findings and assess implementation challenges.To support practical adoption, we recommend a phased deployment strategy beginning with centralised digital platforms that gradually integrate blockchain-based smart contracts as digital readiness improves. Technical implementation should prioritise lightweight and energy-efficient blockchain architectures (e.g., Layer 2 or sidechains) and hybrid edge-cloud AI deployment to handle rural infrastructure constraints. Stakeholder training, regulatory alignment (e.g., GDPR compliance), and governance frameworks involving cooperatives or NGOs will be critical to build trust and ensure inclusive participation. Additionally, to address early-stage data scarcity, we propose transfer learning and synthetic data generation for GenAI training, alongside progressive learning techniques that allow continual adaptation as transaction data accumulates. These avenues represent promising directions to enhance the feasibility and robustness of the proposed approach.

column1: Uncovering Blockchain Adoption Barriers in the Automotive Industry: A Comparative Study of Electric and Traditional Vehicle Manufacturers
column2: Blockchain technology, renowned for its transformative potential in ensuring secure and transparent transactions, plays a crucial role in enhancing efficiency and transparency within the automotive supply chain. This research delves into essential success factors for blockchain integration, employing methodologies like the PESTLE framework, analytic hierarchy process, and Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution. A comprehensive total interpretive structural modeling framework uncovers intricate relationships among factors, while Matriced’Impacts Croises Multiplication Appliquéa un Classement analysis reveals driving and dependence powers. The industry’s movement toward ethical and environmentally conscious practices is evident, though legal, environmental, and technological barriers persist. “Availability of Blockchain Skill Set” and “Education and Awareness” emerge as central factors, emphasizing the symbiotic relationship between a skilled workforce and industry-wide awareness. These factors form the foundation for overcoming barriers, paving the way for seamless blockchain integration in the automotive supply chain. In addition, a comparative analysis between electric vehicle (EV) and traditional automobile manufacturers highlights distinctive priorities, with EV manufacturers focusing on long-term sustainability and transparent supply chains, while traditional automakers strategically approach blockchain adoption, emphasizing education, secure smart contracts, and overcoming adoption challenges.
column3: To summarize, our study highlights the urgent need for the automobile industry to proactively use blockchain technology as a catalyst for increased operational intelligence. Both iterations of the research shed light on the challenging environmental and legal obstacles that must be overcome in order to achieve effective integration. The complex factors of data privacy, security, and smart contract functionality highlight the need for a careful equilibrium between innovation and security. The suggested seven-level hierarchical model and prioritization method are helpful tools for stakeholders, providing guidance in the development of comprehensive plans that tackle economic, technical, social, legal, and environmental concerns. In the future, our study will focus on continuously monitoring the changing blockchain scene in the automobile sector. It is important for researchers and industry leaders to work together to improve and broaden the suggested models, adjusting them to new technical advancements and evolving regulatory environments. Furthermore, examining the practical implementation practices of organizations in the industry and evaluating the enduring effects of incorporating blockchain technology would provide significant observations. Subsequent research might further explore particular differences within different sectors, taking into account variances in variables that influence the adoption of electric vehicles among manufacturers specializing in electric vehicles and those specializing in conventional automobiles. To be at the forefront of blockchain innovation, the automotive sector should adopt a proactive approach and encourage continuous discussion. This will help drive operational efficiency and ensure the industry maintains the highest levels of security, environmental responsibility, and regulatory compliance.

column1: Optimal mode selection strategy for blockchain-enabled remanufacturing trading platform operations: competition vs. cooperation
column2: Remanufacturers are confronted with the dilemma of opting between competition mode (independent sales) and cooperation mode (brand manufacturer channel sales). While the quality of remanufactured products is not inferior to new ones, consumers still remain risk-averse and exhibit skepticism regarding their quality. Blockchain technology, as a new generation of information technology, provides an ideal solution for disclosing quality information about remanufactured products. Along this line, we develop four game models grounded in mean-variance theory, considering both mode selection between remanufacturers and manufacturers and the platform's strategies for adopting blockchain technology. This study reveals that when the quality variance is large and blockchain costs are moderate, it is wiser for the platform not to adopt blockchain. When blockchain costs are low and the environmental impact of remanufactured products is small, both modes are environmentally friendly by adopting blockchain technology. However, when patent license fees are low, the cooperation mode significantly outperforms the competition mode. Furthermore, the impact of consumer search efforts and blockchain on consumer privacy is considered in the extended model, further verifying the robustness of the conclusions. This study offers valuable insights into exploring the optimal mode of product quality information disclosure using emerging technologies in remanufacturing trading platforms.
column3: 7.1. Main findings The main findings of this paper are presented across the following five aspects: Firslty, the optimal choice of competition and cooperation modes depends primarily on patent license fees and quality variance. When the quality variance is relatively small or large, an appropriate patent license fee will induce manufacturers to choose the competition mode. However, in the case of large quality differences, manufacturers will choose the cooperation mode even if they can charge higher patent license fees from the competition mode. Our research discovers that effective collaboration can fully release the potential of remanufacturing in sustainable supply chains (S. Chen et al. Citation 2023). However, in contrast to the conclusions of S. Chen et al. ( Citation 2023), we further reveal that the adoption of blockchain technology can enhance consumer preference for remanufactured products, thereby driving a strategic shift in remanufacturing modes from competition to cooperation. Secondly, whether the platform adopts blockchain technology to disclose quality information has a significant impact on consumers' purchasing decisions. Specifically, it would be counterproductive to disclose insufficient quality information that would in turn erode consumer trust in remanufactured products. However, when blockchain technology is not adopted for quality disclosure, consumers may have a more relaxed attitude towards remanufactured products due to the lack of clear quality information, which in turn favours platforms selling remanufactured products. This ‘fuzzy expectation’ formed by information asymmetry helps to alleviate consumers' concerns about quality to a certain extent, and enhances their acceptance and willingness to purchase remanufactured products. This finding challenges the view put forward by Hou et al. ( Citation 2025) and Tao, Wang, and Zhu ( Citation 2023) that platforms always have a strong incentive to deploy blockchain technology to enhance consumer trust. Our conclusions provide platforms with a more strategic decision to adopt blockchain technology to disclose quality information or not. Thirdly, the environmental friendliness of implementing blockchain technology primarily depends on blockchain costs and the environmental impact of remanufactured products. When blockchain costs are low and the environmental impact factor of remanufactured products is small, or when blockchain costs are high and the environmental impact factor of remanufactured products is large, the adoption of blockchain technology in both the competition and cooperation mode is environmentally friendly. In contrast to Huang et al. ( Citation 2019) and N. Wang et al. ( Citation 2025), who emphasised the environmental impact factors of the remanufacturing model, our study considers the environmental impacts of the cost structure of blockchain technology and its potential for widespread application under two remanufacturing modes. Intuitively, the cooperation mode has an advantage over the competition mode in terms of environmental impacts in the case of higher license fees. This view has been confirmed by many previous studies such as N. Wang et al. ( Citation 2025) and Zhang et al. ( Citation 2024). Nevertheless , our study draws the opposite interesting conclusion. In the case of low patent license fees, the environmental impact of the cooperation mode is always smaller than the competition mode, regardless of whether blockchain technology is adopted. We further consider the essential differences between the two modes in terms of coordination mechanisms. The cooperation mode enables remanufacturers and manufacturers to collaborate to optimise resource utilisation, increase production efficiency and reduce resource waste, thereby significantly reducing negative environmental impacts. Fourthly, when patent license fees are low, the competition mode significantly enhances consumer surplus and social welfare, while higher patent license fees tend to favor the cooperation mode. The influence of blockchain usage costs parallels that of patent license fees: the platform's adoption of blockchain will only benefit consumer surplus and social welfare when the cost of adopting blockchain technology is low. Our conclusions extend to some extent the findings of Hou et al. ( Citation 2025) and Wu, Pu, and Fan ( Citation 2025). They pointed out that the adoption of blockchain technology generally benefits consumer surplus and social welfare. Nevertheless, our study further points out the boundary conditions for such a positive effect, i.e. the level of patent license fees and the cost of blockchain usage are significant determinants of its effectiveness. Finally, some interesting conclusions are also drawn from the four extended models. (a) Considering a higher level of search effort, even if manufacturers are able to gain higher revenue through patent license fees in the competition mode, they remain to choose the cooperative strategy. (b) Faced with the consumer privacy concern effect, when manufacturers choose the competition mode, it is rather more sensible for platforms not to adopt blockchain technology for large quality variance and moderate blockchain cost. This finding contrasts with the view of Hou et al. ( Citation 2025) and Tao, Wang, and Zhu ( Citation 2023) that platforms prefer to adopt blockchain to enhance consumer trust in competitive environments, suggesting that excessive disclosure may instead erode consumer trust in privacy sensitive markets. (c) Conventional wisdom generally holds that dual channels sales are beneficial for manufacturers to maximise profits (Hamzaoui, Turki, and Rezg Citation 2024; Yuan et al. Citation 2025; Zhao and Li Citation 2023). Nevertheless, we discover that when production costs of remanufactured products are moderate, consumer acceptance of online channel is also moderate. Under certain conditions, it may be a superior strategic choice for manufacturers to abandon their own direct sales channels and focus on platform sales. (d) When patent license fees are treated as endogenous decision variables for manufacturers, remanufacturers face greater market pressures as the production costs of remanufactured products and consumer risk aversion increase. To prevent remanufacturers from operating inefficiently or exiting the market, manufacturers will reduce patent license fees to protect their own profits. This is contrary to the conclusion of N. Wang et al. ( Citation 2025) that license fees remained high even though intense competition caused manufacturers to suffer from profitability dilemmas, further revealing the adaptive adjustment mechanism of patent license strategies in a dynamic competitive environment. 7.2. Managerial insights Drawing from the research findings, we further propose the following five managerial insights: Firstly, since the market environment is evolving rapidly, enterprises should routinely assess fluctuations in patent license fees to enable agile strategic adjustments. Confronted with high patent license fees, enterprises should consider increasing investment in R&D to enhance the technical sophistication and added value of their products so as to reduce reliance on license fees. For instance, Apple, confronted with having to pay Qualcomm huge patent license fees, has increased investment in self-developed chips. The M2 Pro/Max chip features a 5nm process, which significantly improves performance and alters the dilemma of Apple's constrained core supply. It can be seen that increasing R&D investment and technological innovation is an effective long-term strategy for enterprises in case of high patent license fees. Secondly, when the quality variance is large and the implementation cost is moderate, it is wiser for platforms to choose not to adopt blockchain. Consequently, platforms like Amazon, Auto barn and Remade Group should consider the impact of product quality variations and implementation costs to choose whether to adopt blockchain technology or not. Additionally, platforms should conduct a comprehensive cost-benefit analysis when adopting blockchain technology, especially for high risk averse consumers. Thirdly, since the targets of cost reductions and efficiency improvements permeate the entire process of remanufacturing, especially in the production chain, platforms should prioritise low-cost blockchain technology to maximise environmental performance and optimise remanufacturing processes. Meanwhile, incorporating blockchain technology into long-term strategic planning will help achieve sustainable development goals and balance economic benefits with environmental responsibility. For instance, remanufacturers can achieve comprehensive tracking and management for product lifecycles with low-cost blockchain technology through Filament's Blocklet system. Additionally, when patent license fees are low, remanufacturers can effectively reduce environmental impacts by choosing the cooperation mode because information sharing and coordination can reduce resource waste. Fourthly, manufacturers should flexibly choose remanufacturing modes in accordance with market environment and cost factors. When patent license fees are low, competition mode can significantly enhance consumer surplus and social welfare. Additionally, blockchain technology serves an essential function in raising awareness among consumers about remanufactured product quality. Nevertheless, prohibitive implementation costs may undermine its effectiveness and militate against maximising environmental performance. Thus, platforms should prioritise low-cost blockchain solutions or reduce implementation costs through technological innovation and scaled adoption, thereby maximising consumer surplus and social welfare while maximising environmental performance for a win-win-win situation. Finally, combining the four extended models, we provide four management insights to manufacturers, remanufacturers, and platforms: (a) Under higher search effort levels, manufacturers and remanufacturers should shift their focus from short-term profit maximisation to long-term maintenance of shared brand value and meet consumer demand for high-quality remanufactured products through collaborative cooperation. (b) Faced with consumer privacy concern, platforms should explore solutions to minimise the disclosure of consumer data in blockchain systems. Meanwhile, manufacturers and remanufacturers should assist platforms in co-shaping a secure and reliable remanufacturing transaction ecosystem. (c) When adopting a dual-channel sales strategy, manufacturers should avoid homogeneous competition between online and offline products. Manufacturers can focus on cost-effective models in online sales and provide personalised services or high-end models in offline sales. (d) Manufacturers should also flexibly adjust patent license fees based on market conditions (e.g. remanufacturing costs, consumer risk aversion, etc.) to achieve both incentives for remanufacturers and market stability. 7.3. Future research Our research can be further extended in the following directions. Firstly, our paper only considers the operational decision-making problems of remanufacturers and manufacturers in a single period. Future research can be extended to two-stage or even multi-stage decision-making problems in the supply chain. Secondly, in practice, manufacturers can remanufacture by themselves and produce both remanufactured and new products at the same time. Therefore, it is also interesting to explore the coexistence of direct sales by manufacturers for self-remanufacturing and online channel sales by platforms in the cooperation mode. Finally, our paper assumes that all consumers are risk-averse, but in reality, there are also risk-neutral or risk-seeking consumers. Consequently, incorporating heterogeneity in consumer risk preferences into discussions will be a valuable direction for future research.

column1: Blockchain implementation decisions in a dual-channel supply chain under different market power structures
column2: The increasing concerns over product safety and adulteration risks have heightened the need for traceability and transparency in supply chains. Blockchain technology provides a potential solution, but its adoption involves costs and strategic decisions about information disclosure. This study investigates a dual-channel supply chain consisting of a supplier and a retailer under four blockchain technology adoption scenarios and two market power structures, where the supplier uses a price-matching policy in the online channel. Stackelberg game models are formulated, and backward induction is used to derive equilibrium decisions on retail price, wholesale price, and amount of blockchain-linked information. The supplier and retailer equilibrium decisions and profits are analyzed and compared across different blockchain technology adoption scenarios and market power structures. Numerical analyses are used to verify the main theoretical results and examine the influences of the parameter values on the equilibrium results. The findings reveal the supplier’s strong incentive to adopt blockchain technology and the retailer’s decision complexity influenced by factors such as consumer shopping convenience, consumer preferences, and retailer competitive position. Additionally, the findings underscore the supplier profitability potential through the traditional retail channel and the value of the price-matching policy to optimise profits for both the supply chain members.
column3: 7.1. Summary This work focuses on a dual-channel supply chain with consumers concerned about product safety and adulteration risks under different market power structures. The supplier and the retailer consider blockchain technology adoption to address the above consumer concerns. The supplier uses the price-matching policy to determine the retail price of the products in the online channel. The market demand functions of different channels are first set up by analyzing the consumer behaviour, and the game models between the supplier and the retailer are formulated. Four different blockchain implementation scenarios and two market power structures are considered and analyzed. The equilibrium profits and decisions are analyzed first under different scenarios with different market power structures. The impacts of the parameter values on the supplier and the retailer profits are then investigated. The Nash equilibrium results are further discussed considering the supplier and the retailer blockchain technology adoption decisions. Finally, extensions of the basic models are explored, and the consistency of the results and the robustness of the basic models are verified, by considering the price competition policy, the different consumer preferences, and the more influential blockchain-linked information on online consumers. 7.2. The main findings and managerial insights The main findings of this work are as follows. First, the supplier has a stronger incentive than the retailer does to adopt blockchain technology. Second, the retailer faces a more nuanced decision-making process, where careful analysis of the market environment, the consumer preferences and its competitive position is essential to make blockchain technology adoption decisions. Third, the supplier has the potential to benefit from the traditional retail channel. Fourth, the supplier price-matching policy is a viable strategy to maximise profits for both of the dual-channel supply chain members. Additionally, aligning blockchain technology adoption with consumer preferences can effectively boost the profits of both the supplier and the retailer. Moreover, the supplier’s profits increase and the retailer’s profits decrease as the influence of blockchain-linked information on online consumers intensifies. Managerial insights obtained from the main findings are summarised as follows: The supplier should proactively explore blockchain technology adoption in the dual channel supply chain to enhance transparency and consumer trust. The supplier can gain significant competitive advantages, increase consumer utility and strengthen its market competitiveness by implementing blockchain technology. Supply chain members, especially the retailer, should conduct comprehensive market analyses to understand the landscape, including consumer preferences, consumer shopping convenience in the retail channel, and its market position for blockchain technology adoption and other operational decisions. The retailer should carefully evaluate the potential benefits and drawbacks of blockchain technology before committing to implementation. The price-matching policy can be an effective strategy for the supplier and the retailer to maximise profits. By matching prices across different sales channels, businesses can retain customers, minimise price competition, and maintain consumer confidence. Aligning blockchain technology adoption with consumer preferences is critical for long-term success. Supply chain members should prioritise consumer-centric approaches, such as enhanced customer service, to meet the evolving needs and expectations of their target consumers. By delivering value to customers, the supplier and the retailer can foster customer loyalty and uphold sustainable growth. 7.3. Future research directions Future research may delve deeper into the impacts of blockchain technology on supply chain resilience and sustainability, considering its potential to enhance transparency and traceability (Beck et al. Citation 2023). Additionally, examining the integration of blockchain with other emerging technologies, such as the Internet of Things and artificial intelligence, may offer insights into more advanced and interconnected supply chain systems (Tiwari et al. Citation 2024). Furthermore, investigating the regulatory and legal implications of blockchain technology adoption in supply chains may provide valuable perspectives for policymakers and industry practitioners. These avenues for future research can contribute to a comprehensive understanding of the implications and applications of blockchain technology in supply chain management. column1: An exploration method for technology forecasting that combines link prediction with graph embedding: A case study on blockchain
column2: To keep pace with the latest technological changes and advancements, predicting future technological trends and topics has become a critical approach for high-tech companies and policy-making institutions. In this paper, we proposed an explorative method that integrates link prediction and Node2Vec graph embedding to predict future technology topics using co-occurrence data from patent keywords. Specifically, this method collects and preprocesses patent datasets, constructs network graphs that depict relationships among different technology topics, and builds a supervised link prediction model based on the time series of the graph to identify future technology graphs. Furthermore, node2vec graph embedding is conducted to obtain node vector representations, and then the clustering algorithms can be improved to identify the relevant topics, which could be interpreted as future technology. A case study on blockchain is conducted to validate the feasibility and practicality of the method to demonstrate the application of the method. Through the comparison of machine learning methods, we selected the Random Forest (RF) model, which presents the highest accuracy, for our experiments. The results show that the proposed method can be used to effectively visualize potential future topics related to a specific technology. Compared to traditional methods such as Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), our method can identify more unique and differentiated technological topics, significantly reducing topic overlap. Additionally, the reported method can illustrate the internal relationships of topics through subgraphs, helping readers better understand the core concepts of each topic and vividly displaying the structure and composition of the topics. Furthermore, the proposed method can also depict potential relationships between different technology topics, which can facilitate the visualization of new directions of research and development.
column3: 5 Conclusions and discussion Basically, technology/innovation forecasting or technological opportunity analysis is a typically systematic process; however, qualitative or quantitative methods can play important roles, and many relevant studies in recent decades have presented their advantages. The development process of quantitative methods for technology forecasting can be divided into the following phases: ( I ) quasiquantitative, ( II ) bibliometric and patent analysis, ( III ) text mining and statistical machine learning (pre-AI era), ( IV ) large language models (LLM) and deep learning (post-AI era). Today, the research schema on technology forecasting can experience a transition from phase III to phase IV , and the proposed method for technology forecasting based on network link prediction and node2vec graph embedding also depicts this change or evolution. Semantic computing in large-scale knowledge graphs was challenged and intractable until LLM and deep learning models were developed and reported. In this paper, a new method to predict future technological topics is proposed through the use of supervised link prediction and node2vec-based analysis. By analyzing co-occurrence data from patents, the method generates a network graph that represents the relationships between different technology topics. The graph is subsequently used to identify clusters of related topics, which are interpreted as future technology themes. The method is demonstrated by using a case study of blockchain technology and identifying key themes and their interrelatedness, validating the feasibility and practicality of the method. The method proposed in this article further enriches the tools for technology forecasting and strategic planning and brings forward a new perspective to broaden the methodology related to technology or innovation opportunity forecasting. Compared with some traditional methods for topic discovery or prediction, combining link prediction of knowledge networks with node2vec graph embedding yields moderately good results. By identifying future technology themes, organizations can prepare for emerging trends and allocate resources effectively. The strength of the proposed method lies in its ability to uncover latent relationships between different technology topics, which may not be apparent to domain experts. By analyzing co-occurrence data, the method can identify topics that are likely to emerge together in the future. Moreover, this paper selects only 1-g as the keyword, and n-grams will be considered in the future so that the meaning of technical words can be more accurately understood. However, the reported work in this paper has several limitations. First, while our method requires a moderately large dataset of relevant patents to generate a robust network graph Second, the method relies on the assumption that co-occurrence of key words in patents indicates a relationship between technology topics, which is explorative and could be controversial comparing with the traditional co-occurrence of IPC codes ( Wu et al., 2023 ). Actually, the co-occurrence does not always imply a true technological relationship and may be influenced by non-technical factors. Nevertheless, our case study on blockchain has shown that this assumption holds well in this particular field, demonstrating the moderate validity and effectiveness. In future work, more case studies are needed to further refine this assumption to improve its applicability across various domains. One potential direction in the sequential research is to explore alternative data sources, such as academic papers or social media posts, to supplement the patent data. Additionally, more deep learning techniques and models could be used to analyze the data and identify relationships beyond co-occurrence. In fact, in the age of artificial intelligence, not only is the analytical schema of technology forecasting changing; however, the methodology of scientific study and discovery can also face dramatic shifting, and the schema of artificial intelligence for science (AI4S) is rising ( Messeri and Crockett, 2024 ).

column1: Profit or prestige? Strategies for luxury brands to navigate the second-hand market using blockchain technology
column2: Luxury brands are increasingly adopting blockchain technology to combat counterfeiting, yet they face a dilemma in addressing the market of second-hand luxury products. While a luxury brand's involvement in second-hand sales could diminish its exclusivity, it could also increase the brand's profits. Motivated by luxury brands’ concerns about venturing into the second-hand market while preserving their brand exclusivity, this study presents an analytical model to investigate how blockchain authentication impacts their strategies in the second-hand market. A distinctive feature of this study is the conceptualisation of aspirational value associated with the luxury brand. Our analysis reveals that premium and mass-market brands can improve brand exclusivity by enhancing second-hand product quality. However, luxury brands may diminish brand exclusivity if the quality of second-hand products is high. Additionally, luxury brands can maintain exclusivity by avoiding the second-hand market when using blockchain for authentication, provided that the authentication cost is below a threshold. Furthermore, our research sheds light on the strategies of various fashion brands (mass-market, premium, and luxury brands), contingent upon their aspirational values, to combat counterfeit products by deploying a blockchain-based authentication mechanism for the second-hand market.
column3: 5 Conclusion 5.1 Theoretical implications From a theoretical perspective, this research contributes to two streams of literature: second-hand platforms and the use of blockchain technology to authenticate luxury products. While prior studies have explored these topics separately, they have not specifically examined the simultaneous impact of blockchain on brand exclusivity and brand profitability in the second-hand market ( Shen et al., 2020, 2021 ). This study addresses that gap by using a single-period game-theoretic analytical model to analyse brand-appropriate strategies for blockchain technology in the second-hand market, considering factors such as the social value attached to knowingly purchasing counterfeits, the brand’s aspirational value, and status utility. Our findings provide valuable insights for luxury brand managers regarding the role of blockchain technology, luxury identity, and product quality in preserving brand exclusivity, as well as the circumstances under which the second-hand platform can impact the brand’s aspirational value. By shedding light on these issues, this study may inspire further research in this area and provide a foundation for developing future effective strategies for luxury brands.

column1: Blockchain adoption of pharmaceutical firms in a competitive market: Pricing, drug traceability and consumer awareness
column2: To cope with counterfeit drugs reaching consumers all over the world, pharmaceutical firms increasingly regard blockchain technology (BCT) as a promising solution to achieve drug traceability. This study proposes a game-theoretic model to investigate the impact of BCT adoption on pharmaceutical firms’ pricing and performance in a competitive market, where one firm offers a branded drug and the other offers a generic version. We consider three contrastive cases with no BCT adoption, unilateral BCT adoption of the branded drug firm and bilateral BCT adoption and characterize consumer traceability awareness, which represents the fraction of consumers sensitive to drug traceability. We find that when BCT is unilaterally adopted, a high consumer traceability awareness level may lead to either higher or lower drug prices. The bilateral adoption of BCT always benefits the generic drug firm due to the enhanced drug traceability, but may damage the branded drug firm attributed to the mitigated differentiation between the two drugs. Compared with the unilateral adoption of BCT, bilaterally adopting BCT can lead to a win-win or lose-lose outcome, depending on the trade-off of drug traceability, drug differentiation and pricing competition. In addition, the adoption of BCT improves consumer welfare when consumers hold a high level of traceability awareness.
column3: 2.4 Summary of the literature We summarize the differences between this work and the extant literature to highlight our academic contributions. First, we complement the existing studies by examining the impacts of drug traceability and BCT adoption on the pricing of branded and generic drugs in the off-patent market. Second, several critical characteristics of drugs and consumers in the pharmaceutical market, such as drug authentic probability and consumer heterogeneity in drug traceability awareness, are considered and their impacts on pharmaceutical firms' pricing and performance are investigated. Third, a game-theoretic model is developed to study the impacts of BCT adoption on pharmaceutical firms’ pricing and performance in a competitive market, which is generally explored descriptively by the previous studies. To the best of our knowledge, these issues have not been addressed in the literature before.

column1: Blockchain-Based Governance: Implications for Organizational Boundaries and Structures
column2: Blockchain has emerged as a key Industry 4.0 technology, enabling novel forms of governance and coordination mechanism among organizations and markets. However, extant literature has largely focused on the technical aspects of blockchain, with limited attention to the behavioural and institutional aspects. In this paper, we argue that blockchain‐based smart contracts and decentralized autonomous organizations represent the potential for a radical departure from traditional forms of contractual governance and hierarchy, carrying profound implications for the design and governance of economic transaction and organizational structures. We elucidate how blockchain technologies, characterized by transparency, immutability, programmability and decentralization, reduce transaction costs and establish an industrialized and trustless transactional governance system. Finally, we present an agenda for future research, highlighting the need for new theoretical frameworks and empirical evidence to understand the impact of blockchain on organizational design and forms.
column3: In conclusion, the integration of blockchain technology into the realm of organizational governance has ushered in a new era of possibilities and challenges for organizational research. As we elucidated, blockchain's potential goes beyond mere efficiency enhancement, extending to the transformation of traditional structures and trust mechanisms. Future research should delve into the intricate dynamics of blockchain's impact on decision-making processes, exploring the scalability challenges, competitive advantages and potential coexistence of decentralized autonomous organizations with established hierarchies. Further, the confluence of blockchain with other Industry 4.0 technologies, such as AI/ML, marks a pivotal moment in the evolution of organizational design, promising both disruption and innovation. As organizations adapt to this rapidly changing landscape, it is clear that understanding and harnessing the full potential of Industry 4.0 technologies will be a critical endeavour for scholars and practitioners alike.

column1: Building trust takes time: limits to arbitrage for blockchain-based assets
column2: A blockchain replaces central counterparties with time-consuming consensus protocols to record the transfer of ownership. This settlement latency slows cross-exchange trading, exposing arbitrageurs to price risk. Off-chain settlement, instead, exposes arbitrageurs to costly default risk. We show with Bitcoin network and order book data that cross-exchange price differences coincide with periods of high settlement latency, asset flows chase arbitrage opportunities, and price differences across exchanges with low default risk are smaller. Blockchain-based trading thus faces a dilemma: Reliable consensus protocols require time-consuming settlement latency, leading to arbitrage limits. Circumventing such arbitrage costs is possible <italic>only</italic> by reinstalling trusted intermediation, which mitigates default risk.
column3:
Many market participants believe that blockchain technologies have the potential to radi­
cally transform the transfer of financial assets. Replacing trusted intermediaries and central
clearing parties with blockchain technologies may increase efficiency and security and may
lower transaction costs. However, new frictions emerge for blockchain-based assets as the
potential merits come at the cost of latency in the settlement process. The inability to per­
form instantaneous cross-exchange transactions implies limits to arbitrage as market par­
ticipants cannot react sufficiently fast to potential violations of the law of one price.
 We show that settlement latency implies limits to arbitrage as it is not incentive-
compatible for risk-averse arbitrageurs to exploit cross-exchange price differences in peri­
ods with high volatility and long validation times. We formally derive the resulting no-
trade price bounds for concave utility functions and a general class of latency distributions.
 Using data from the Bitcoin market in 2018 and 2019, we show that price differences re­
main large during periods of high spot volatility, settlement latency, and settlement latency
uncertainty. Cross-exchange net flows chase price differences, which indicates that market
participants perceive these restrictions.
 These results shed new light on the inherent trade-off between the costs and benefits of
central clearing versus blockchain-based settlement. While central clearing counterparties
take on counterparty risk to guarantee instantaneous trading on non-settled positions,
blockchains render trusted intermediation obsolete. However, the degree of trustworthi­
ness for blockchain-based assets depends on the validation process’s complexity, which ul­
timately causes settlement latency. We document the substantial economic costs of latency-
related trading frictions for blockchain-based assets.
 To put arbitrage capital under an exchange’s custody and rely on an exchange’s protec­
tion against counterparty risk by providing collateral requires the trustworthiness of the

exchange. Though we observe an increase in trust in exchanges, measured by the increase
in funds under the custody of exchanges, our results indicate that intermediation services
are still insufficiently utilized to exploit cross-exchange price differences. Frequent occur­
rences of centralized exchange defaults are a vivid reminder of these default risks.

 In fact, we demonstrate that settlement latency remains a statistically and economically
significant driving force of time-varying price differences, even when we control for
exchange-specific inventory holdings and margin trading possibilities. These results indi­
cate that circumventing settlement latency via alternative strategies is not sufficiently perva­
sive to offset the impact of arbitrage bounds completely. A possible reason is a lack of trust
in the capabilities of CEXes to serve as central counterparties.
 This article thus contributes to an ongoing debate on the organization of clearing on fi­
nancial markets and the role of third-party intermediation for reliable settlement systems.
Our analysis demonstrates that a decentralized system cannot easily replace central clear­
ing. Removing the frictions (and costs) induced by third-party intermediation causes novel
trading frictions with non-trivial implications for pricing. First, limits to arbitrage implied
by settlement latency may harm price efficiency, as the lower activity of arbitrageurs
reduces the information flow across exchanges. Second, deviations from the law of one
price affect the pricing of assets, as risk-neutral probabilities are not uniquely defined.
Third, the implied costs of settlement latency depend on the design of the blockchain and
should influence the decision of whether to migrate to a decentralized settlement system.

column1: Implications of Blockchain-Powered Marketplace of Preowned Virtual Goods
column2: The first‐sale doctrine, which protects consumers’ rights to resell purchased products, has been recognized by the US Supreme Court since 1908. In recent years, consumers have begun to purchase an increasing amount of virtual goods, which renders the first‐sale doctrine unclear. There are two main challenges leading to the uncertainty of the first‐sale doctrine in the digital age: lack of proper technology, and economic implications for developers and consumers. The advent of the blockchain solves the technology challenge, as it can track provenance and establish the chain of custody. In this study, we construct an analytical model to investigate the economic impact of trading preowned virtual items. Specifically, our model captures the decentralized nature of blockchain technology by allowing consumer‐to‐consumer trading, and considers the possibility that consumers prefer preowned virtual items over new ones because preowned items may be upgraded between purchase and resale. Lawmakers seek to strike a balance between the interests of virtual item developers and individual consumers. We show that, surprisingly, the introduction of a blockchain‐based preowned virtual item transaction can actually benefit both developer and consumer. The main intuition is that the developer can adjust the price when forward‐looking consumers incorporate the expected future transaction into their purchase decision. Our analysis also reveals that developers are more willing to embrace the secondary market when they can take a cut during the transaction. Our results provide important policy implications to the burgeoning debate of the first‐sale doctrine in the new digital world.
column3: In this paper, we study the implications of the transaction of preowned virtual items. Our research is motivated by the ongoing debate of the applicability of the first-sale doctrine in the digital world. The first-sale doctrine has been protecting consumers’ interests for over a century by allowing individual consumers to trade their used items, but technology has changed the environment dramatically because it was first established. Due to unreliable technology concerns and uncertainty of economic implications, lawmakers are hesitant to adopt the first-sale doctrine in a digital world. This is a representative issue concerning whether old laws should be reinterpreted to adapt to evolving technology.The emergence of blockchain technology has resolved the piracy and technological issues of digital resales by allowing developers to track provenance and chain of custody. Virtual item developers have been embracing this technology, which allows true ownership for virtual item consumers. Despite the popularity of trading used virtual items, its economic impact remains unclear. To respond, we construct an analytical model to investigate the implication of used virtual item trading on developers and consumers. Specifically, our two-period model captures a unique feature of virtual items: They can be upgraded after purchase, so used items may have greater value than new ones. As a result, consumers in the later period prefer the used virtual item to the new item. We also capture the decentralized nature of blockchain technology by allowing consumers to trade virtual items directly among each other. The setup of our model allows the main insights to take center stage rather than the technical complexities inherent to a more general model.Our research reveals several important and interesting theoretical findings. First, our study shows that the introduction of preowned virtual item trading can improve the profitability of the developer under certain conditions. This result is quite surprising in the sense that physical goods suppliers can never become better off by introducing a secondary market for used items. For virtual items, the competition between preowned products and new products is fiercer than for physical products, as consumers may prefer upgraded preowned items to new items. The main intuition driving the result is that consumers are forward-looking and can anticipate the potential increase in trade value of virtual items in the later periods, which incentivizes early consumers to pay a premium in the first period. Moreover, we find that the developer's gain is not at the cost of the consumer. Our results show that consumer surplus will actually increase with the introduction of preowned virtual item trading. The main intuition of this result is that first-period consumers have the opportunity to trade their preowned virtual items, while second-period consumers benefit directly from the introduction of preowned virtual items because it drives down the price of new items. Another interesting finding has to do with the impact of the revenue sharing proportion. We consider an alternative setting in which the developer can take a cut of the transaction of a preowned virtual item. We find that the developer is more willing to embrace blockchain technology to facilitate the transaction of preowned virtual items, as this gives them a second stream of revenue on top of selling the new items alone. However, our analysis also reveals that the developer's profit does not monotonically increase in the revenue sharing proportion that the developer can keep; when the revenue sharing proportion becomes too high, it will discourage the consumer's purchase in the first period, which hurts the developer.Our study also provides significant and relevant insights for policymakers and regulators. To begin with, our study sheds light on the impact of preowned virtual item transactions on developers and consumers. It provides evidence that extending the first-sale doctrine to the digital world can always benefit the consumer but may or may not improve the profitability of the developer. To balance the interest between the developer and consumer, our results suggest that regulators can delegate the right to the developer. It should be the developer's choice whether or not to introduce blockchain technology to facilitate the transaction of preowned virtual items. If the developer chooses not to allow the transaction of preowned virtual items, she can impose a license instead of selling when transferring the virtual item to a new consumer. In this scenario, the consumer can use but not trade the item. Second, we find that allowing the developer to take a cut during the transaction can further incentivize her to accept the resale of virtual items. The implication of this result is that if lawmakers are leaning toward adapting the first-sale doctrine for virtual items, they may need to revise the doctrine to allow the developer to take a cut of the transaction of the preowned virtual item. Finally, although we focus on virtual goods in this study, which are used mainly in online communities and games, the implication can also resonate with other, broader categories of digital goods including digital books, music, movies, and other digital goods.We briefly note a few limitations of this study and provide some directions for future research. To begin with, we consider a two-period model to simplify the analysis and facilitate comparisons. Future research can extend the current study to a multiple-period or continuous-time setting to analyze the nuance of dynamic pricing in this setting. Second, based on the practice, we focus on the situation that the developer reaches the consumer directly through her own platform or through a third-party platform. It may be interesting to consider other incentive contracts in this setting. Third, to gain sharp insights, we focus on the scenario in which the upgrade ratio across all consumers is identical. An interesting direction for exploration is to investigate the impact of the heterogeneity of upgrade ratio on developer's profit and consumer surplus. Fourth, to ensure the analytical clarity, we abstract away the setup cost of blockchain technology. Future research should look into the impact of the setup cost on preowned virtual goods marketplace. Notwithstanding these limitations, the current study presents the first step in understanding how the introduction of blockchain technology may affect developer profit and consumer surplus, and contributes to the burgeoning debate of the first-sale doctrine in the new digital world.

column1: A structured literature review on the interplay between emerging technologies and COVID-19 â€“ insights and directions to operations fields
column2: In recent years, emerging technologies have gained popularity and being implemented in different fields. Thus, critical leading-edge technologies such as artificial intelligence and other related technologies (blockchain, simulation, 3d printing, etc.) are transforming the operations and other traditional fields and proving their value in fighting against unprecedented COVID-19 pandemic outbreaks. However, due to this relation's novelty, little is known about the interplay between emerging technologies and COVID-19 and its implications to operations-related fields. In this vein, we mapped the extant literature on this integration by a structured literature review approach and found essential outcomes. In addition to the literature mapping, this paper's main contributions were identifying literature scarcity on this hot topic by operations-related fields; consequently, our paper emphasizes an urgent call to action. Also, we present a novel framework considering the primary emerging technologies and the operations processes concerning this pandemic outbreak. Also, we provided an exciting research agenda and four propositions derived from the framework, which are collated to operations processes angle. Thus, scholars and practitioners have the opportunity to adapt and advance the framework and empirically investigate and validate the propositions for this and other highly disruptive crisis.
column3: In this study, we explored the interplay between emerging technologies and COVID-19 by means of a structured literature review, taking into account the operations-related fields. Thus, our findings showed that cutting-edge AI technologies like machine learning and deep learning are the most popular approaches to support operations in this pandemic outbreak, but that other related technologies—like big data analytics, blockchain, simulation, AR/VR, 3d printing, etc.—are also increasingly since the outbreak of COVID-19. Findings also indicate that a group of leading-edge technologies (i.e., digital twin, 5G, drones, etc.) remain at their infancy stage when it comes to interventions or applications in emergency situations. Similarly, it appears that all these technologies, together with more others, are mainly used in operations related to contact tracing, telemedicine, diagnosis, drug repurposing, forecasting, etc. In terms of contributions, this study appears as one of the first papers that have mapped the literature exploring key emerging technologies in the COVID-19 outlook. Secondly, we found that traditional journals featured very few papers dealing with the production and operations fields. This therefore reinforces the need for scholars and practitioners to call for action so that this gap be filled. Thirdly, we provided a novel framework that synthesizes the main emerging technologies that can be used in the context of a huge epidemic outbreak. Fourthly, the four propositions derived from the framework can be a rich avenue for scholars and practitioners to investigate and empirically validate the role of emerging technologies in emergency situations. Lastly, we suggest other exciting future research directions supported by key organizational theories and OR/OM approaches.

column1: Carbon trading price forecasting in digitalization social change era using an explainable machine learning approach: The case of China as emerging country evidence
column2: Carbon trading prices are considered important reference indicators for policy formulation and enterprise decision-making, and play an important role in low-carbon development. However, predictive approaches that balance the accuracy and interpretability of carbon trading prices remain limited. This study proposes a hybrid approach that integrates group variable selection regularization and uncertainty inference in Bayesian neural networks (BNN) with inherent interpretability to predict carbon trading prices. We also identify effective predictive indicators in an emerging market context. Based on the carbon data of emerging markets, a dataset of price information was constructed for model training. The results indicate that under the same regularized dataset, all BNN results surpass other artificial neural networks (ANNs). The group smoothly clipped absolute deviation-BNN performs best in all models and has interpretability. The model effectively identified new influencing factors for predicting carbon trading prices in emerging countries, including coal prices and blockchain-related information. The proposed new prediction approach provides a new basis for the prediction and evaluation of carbon trading prices and provides the necessary references for policy formulation in the digitalization era of social change.
column3: 6 Conclusion To predict carbon trading prices in the era of digitalization and social change, we propose an interpretable machine learning approach with the Chinese context as a case study. Specifically, a novel parametric norm penalty regularization-BNN framework is proposed, which integrates the group variable method Group LASSO and Group SCAD variable screening methods and inputs the screened indicators into the interpretable BNN. In addition, group variable screening methods such as parameter norm penalties are applied to innovatively and effectively screen blockchain information indicators and the price of thermal coal from the Bohai Sea in China as an emerging country context. The experimental results show that compared with the traditional artificial neural network model, the proposed Group SCAD-BNN approach can make more effective use of carbon trading price time-series data information, reduce overfitting, and improve prediction accuracy and interpretability. Under the three-parameter norm penalty method, BNN was superior to ANN. This study uses the proposed inherently interpretable machine learning approach to fit time-series data of carbon trading price fluctuations and conducts prediction research. Thus, our study extends the knowledge of interpretable machine learning approaches and fills a gap in the application of these approaches to carbon trading price prediction. The new prediction approach and proposed theoretical ecology provide a new basis for trend prediction and the evaluation of time series represented by the carbon trading price. It also provides a necessary reference for policy-making and decision-making by specific stakeholders.

column1: The (Limited) Power of Blockchain Networks for Information Provision
column2: We investigate the potential and limits of privacy-preserving corporate blockchain applications for information provision. We provide a theoretical model in which heterogeneous firms choose between adopting a blockchain application or relying on traditional third-party intermediaries to inform the capital market. The blockchain’s ability to generate information depends on each firm’s data profile and all firms’ endogenous adoption decisions. We show that blockchain technology can improve the information environment and outperform traditional institutions with firms’ adoption decisions serving as a credible value signal and the application uncovering firm values by analyzing all participating firms’ data. However, we also characterize an adverse mixed-adoption equilibrium in which neither of the two channels realizes its full potential and information provision declines not only for individual firms, but also in aggregate. The equilibrium is a warning sign that has broad implications for policymakers’ regulatory effort and investors’ assessment of corporate blockchain applications.
