column1: Can government policies help to achieve the pollutant emissions information disclosure target in the Industry 4.0 era?
column2: In the Industry 4.0 era, manufacturers commonly adopt digital technologies such as Internet of Things (IoT) and blockchain technology to improve information disclosure. In this paper, we focus on how the government can properly set an extended producer responsibility (EPR) policy (penalty or subsidy) and impose it on the manufacturer to entice the manufacturer to set the optimal pollutant emissions information disclosure (PEID) level which maximizes the social welfare. In the basic model, we build a simple consumer utility based stylized analytical model. We first derive from the government perspective the social welfare function and obtain the closed-form expression of the optimal level of PEID. Then, we explore the manufacturer’s problem on PEID under the EPR policy. We show how the EPR policy can be set so that the government can entice the manufacturer to set the PEID level which maximizes the social welfare. We also uncover the factors governing the EPR policy, and show the situations under which the EPR policy is in fact a subsidy scheme (i.e., the government sponsors the manufacturer). To derive more insights and check for robustness, we extend the basic model in a number of ways, namely (i) the situation when the manufacturer is risk sensitive, (ii) the case with the extended consumer responsibility (ECR) policy, (iii) the scenario when there is a per unit PEID level dependent operating cost (i.e., a variable cost), and (iv) the case when the platform is not supported by blockchain. We find that the form of EPR policy and the qualitative insights remain valid for the cases when the manufacturer is risk sensitive and there is a PEID level dependent operating cost. Interestingly, we uncover that, unlike the EPR policy, the use of ECR policy fails to help.
column3: In the blockchain era, digital technologies such as Internet of Things (IoT) and blockchain are crucial to support sustainable operations. In this paper, motivated by the observed practices, we examine how the government can properly set an EPR policy, which can be a penalty tax or subsidy based scheme, to entice the manufacturer to set the social welfare maximizing pollutant emissions information disclosure (PEID) level. In the basic model, we establish a simple consumer utility based stylized analytical model and derive the social welfare function. We then obtain the closed-form analytical expression of the social welfare maximizing level of PEID. Then, we explore the manufacturer’s problem on PEID under the EPR policy and derive the optimal PEID level from the manufacturer’s perspective. After that, we analytically show how the EPR policy can be set so that the government can entice the manufacturer to set the PEID level which maximizes the social welfare. We also reveal how different important factors affect the EPR policy. To derive more insights and check for robustness, we extend the basic model in a number of ways and generate various insights. In the following, we discuss some important findings and their managerial implications. 5.1 Social welfare maximizing PEID The level of manufacturing pollution emissions, the manufacturing cost and the cost coefficient of improving the PEID level are all key factors which influence the social welfare maximizing PEID level (see Proposition 1). However, it is a bit surprising to note that the social welfare optimizing PEID level is independent of the selling price. These features of the social welfare maximizing PEID indicate that when the government sets this PEID target, special attention has to be paid to the level of manufacturing pollution emissions and the product’s manufacturing cost, but not the product’s selling price. 5.2 Manufacturer’s optimal PEID Different from the social welfare maximizing PEID, the product’s selling price is a critical factor which affects the manufacturer’s optimal PEID level (Proposition 2). Similar to the social welfare maximizing PEID level, both the manufacturing cost and the PEID cost coefficient of improving the PEID level are critical factors affecting the manufacturer’s optimal PEID level. In addition, under the EPR policy, if the government imposes an EPR tax/subsidy, then a larger EPR tax/subsidy implies a smaller PEID level. 5.3 Optimal EPR policy The optimal EPR policy can be either a penalty taxation scheme or a subsidy scheme (Proposition 3). Whether it should be a penalty taxation scheme or a subsidy scheme depends on the magnitude of environmental impact (which is measured by the level of manufacturing pollution emissions). When the level of manufacturing pollution emissions is not sufficiently big, the government should establish the optimal EPR policy that provides an incentive to the manufacturer to sponsor its PEID, rather than charging a penalty tax. 5.4 Risk sensitive manufacturer First, we find that a more risk prone manufacturer is willing to set a higher PEID level than the less risk prone counterpart (P.S.: Also including risk neutral and risk averse). Second, when the manufacturer is risk prone or risk averse, the optimal EPR policy exhibits a similar form as the case with a risk neutral manufacturer (except that the critical threshold 𝜃 ^ 𝑅 𝑖 𝑠 𝑘 is different and it depends on the manufacturer’s risk sensitivity). In particular, if the manufacturer is more risk prone, 𝜃 ^ 𝑅 𝑖 𝑠 𝑘 is smaller which implies that the likelihood of having a penalty taxation scheme as the optimal EPR policy is higher. Second, it is found that if the manufacturer is more risk prone, whether the optimal EPR tax/subsidy e under the EPR policy is larger or smaller depends on the level of manufacturing pollution emissions. If the level of manufacturing pollution emissions is sufficiently big (resp. small), then a larger (resp. smaller) e is needed to entice the manufacturer to invest according to the social welfare maximizing PEID level when the manufacturer is more risk prone. 5.5 Extended consumer responsibility Our finding shows that the ECR policy is not useful to help entice the manufacturer to achieve the social welfare maximizing PEID target (Proposition 6). Thus, the government should not consider it in our problem setting. This finding has very important practical implications and it may explain why in practice, most environmental policies mainly focus on EPR, rather than ECR. 5.6 The presence of a unit PEID dependent operating cost Considering the presence of a unit operating cost for using the blockchain based platform for PEID, we reveal that the findings are very similar to the case in which this cost is not present (or assumed to be trivial). This implies that our derived findings in the simple basic model are in fact valid under the more general case. 5.7 Blockchain or other technologies We uncover that if an alternative technology is used instead of blockchain, the resulting social welfare maximizing PEID level will drop, which is not desirable. We hence propose that blockchain should be the major technology to serve the purpose of establishing the PEID platform (if the manufacturer has sufficient resources to justify the initial investment which is a sunk cost that we do not consider in our operations model). Future studies can be conducted for exploring more on how digital technologies can be used to support platform operations (Liu et al., 2022) with the specific goal of enhancing environmental sustainability. Other studies can explore the more complex production systems such as those with multiple stages or multiple periods. The corresponding required EPR policy which can achieve the desirable sustainability related target may take a much more complex form.

column1: Fine-grained digital twin sharing framework for smart construction through an incentive mechanism
column2: Prefabricated construction is increasingly applied in the construction industry. Recent academic and industrial efforts highlight that Digital Twin as a Service (DTaaS) is an innovative solution to strengthen the advantages of prefabricated construction by enabling continuous monitoring, precise control, and optimized maintenance of each unique module. However, the complexity of digital twins presents significant challenges for both platforms and subcontractors to apply and fully understand this technology. It is, therefore, crucial to develop a well-designed sharing environment where stakeholders volunteer to share their digital twin resources for synergistic benefits. This research proposes an innovative blockchain-based fine-grained digital twin sharing framework, with detailed architecture focused on two key stages of prefabricated construction: on-site construction and logistics involving warehousing and transport. An incentive mechanism is introduced to encourage all the stakeholders engaged in digital twin sharing framework to contribute and share more digital twin resources. Evolutionary and cooperative games explore the effective settings of the incentive policies, aiming to ensure the feasibility and sustainability of the proposed system by motivating users to share digital twins with fine granularity. Mathematical and numerical results demonstrate the optimal subsidy policies with/without budgetary constraints and further highlight the effectiveness of well-crafted incentives. Findings reveal that better performance in terms of profitability and digital twin sharing is achieved under the proposed incentives. Subsidies are primarily allocated to offset costs with a certain budget, whereas the emphasis shifts towards quality improvement under an ample budget. This study lays a solid foundation for digital twin reuse and development.
column3: 2.4 Summary and research gap The complexity of digital twins makes it difficult for subcontractors in the prefabrication industry to apply this innovation, and for developers to fully understand the interdisciplinary models contained in digital twins. Therefore, it is important to develop a well-designed sharing environment that breaks down the complexity of digital twins and allows participants to contribute to digital twins in a fine-grained form to improve reusability, scalability, and maintainability. More importantly, how to promote the willingness of subcontractors to share is the key question. Incentives should be well developed considering three fields of warehousing, transportation, and construction in a planned manner to avoid participants only sharing easily generated technologies or knowledge, resulting in unbalanced sharing. While existing studies have extensively explored the use of evolutionary and cooperative game theory in designing incentive mechanisms for various applications, there remains a significant gap in the literature regarding incentives for sharing fine-grained digital twins. Current research focuses on the quantity of shared DT resources ( Li et al., 2023 ), without adequately addressing the quality of sharing, particularly as measured by the instantiation level. This paper addresses this gap by proposing an innovative incentive mechanism that considers both the quantity and quality of shared digital twins, which promotes effective collaboration and enhances productivity in smart construction. Numerous studies concern the prefabrication industry, but few attempted to integrate deep expertise and technology for the development of smart prefabricated construction, which would provide professional, efficient, personalized, and innovative services. Hence, proposing a professional digital twin sharing framework through well-designed incentive measures fills the research in prefabrication construction.

column1: Blockchain=better food? The adoption of blockchain technology in food supply chain
column2:
Purpose
This study aims to investigate the integration of blockchain technology into the food supply chain within the restaurant industry. It focuses on how blockchain can be applied to enhance transparency and trust in tracking food sources, ultimately impacting customer satisfaction.

Design/methodology/approach
A service design workshop (Study 1) and three between-subjects experiments (Studies 2–4) were conducted.

Findings
Results indicate that blockchain adoption significantly improves traceability and trust in the food supply chain. This improvement in turn enhances customer satisfaction through perceived improvements in food safety, quality and naturalness. This study also notes that the effects of blockchain technology vary depending on the type of restaurant (casual or fine dining) and its location (tourist destinations or residential areas).

Practical implications
The findings offer practical insights for restaurant owners, technology developers and policymakers. Emphasizing the benefits of blockchain adoption, this study guides decision-making regarding technology investments for enhancing customer service and satisfaction in the hospitality sector.

Originality/value
This research contributes novel insights to the field of technology innovation in the hospitality industry. It extends the understanding of signaling theory by exploring how blockchain technology can serve as a tool for signal transmission in restaurant food supply chains.
column3: Four studies highlight the importance of blockchain adoption in the F&B industry to enhance traceability, trust, and ultimately improve customer satisfaction. Study 1 emphasizes the value of blockchain in traceability and trust, showing that adopting blockchain enhances food perceptions (safety, quality, and naturalness) and improves the customer dining experience, depending on the restaurant type and location. Studies 2, 3, and 4 confirm that blockchain adoption significantly increases traceability and trust, which in turn positively influence food safety, quality, naturalness, and customer satisfaction. Furthermore, studies 3 and 4 examine the moderation effects of restaurant types and locations, suggesting that the impact of blockchain adoption on traceability and trust varies, with more pronounced effects observed in casual dining and tourist destinations. 7.2 Theoretical implications This study advances knowledge in the field of hospitality technology by examining the application of blockchain in the industry. While previous research has recognized benefits like cost reductions, efficiency improvements, and quality control (Treiblmaier & Garaus, 2023; Yong et al., 2020), limited research has focused on the customer perspective regarding blockchain traceability. The adoption of blockchain represents a significant technological advancement in the F&B industry, with the potential to revolutionize restaurant operations. By investigating stakeholder perceptions and attitudes towards this technology, the study sheds light on the potential benefits of blockchain adoption, such as enhanced traceability and trust. The findings offer insights for future research and development in the hospitality industry, contributing to its overall growth and sustainability. Second, this study contributes to signaling theory by emphasizing the importance of blockchain adoption in signaling the commitment of restaurants to food safety, quality, and naturalness. Signaling theory suggests that companies use signals to convey their commitment to certain values and goals, and the adoption of blockchain can act as a signal of a restaurant's commitment to these values (Connelly et al., 2011). The findings of this study suggest that blockchain adoption can improve customer perceptions of food safety, quality, and naturalness, thereby increasing their satisfaction with the restaurant. Importantly, these findings identify blockchain-based traceability systems as signals of customer food perceptions, influencing their attitude and behavior, which aligns with previous studies (Treiblmaier & Garaus, 2023). Third, the study highlights the value of service design workshops as a methodology for understanding customer preferences and needs in the F&B industry. Service design workshops 20 were chosen due to their exploratory, user-oriented, creative, and collaborative nature (Font et al., 2021). By emphasizing experiences, needs, and values, and integrating multiple data collection methods, these workshops provide a comprehensive understanding of participants' attitudes and perceptions (Font et al., 2021). They serve as effective tools for designing and implementing new services or technologies in the F&B industry. The collaborative and creative nature of these workshops fosters the generation of innovative ideas, contributing to the industry's development. Fourth, the study contributes to the understanding of the relationship between restaurant type and location and the adoption of blockchain. The findings suggest that casual dining restaurants and restaurants located in tourist destinations may be more likely to adopt blockchain and benefit from its impact on traceability and trust, while fine dining and restaurants located in residential areas may not experience as significant of an impact. 7.3 Managerial implications This study has significant managerial implications that go beyond its theoretical contributions. First, it emphasizes the potential of tracking and verifying the safety, quality, and naturalness of food ingredients in the F&B industry to enhance traceability and build trust with customers. These efforts can foster improved business relationships and generate increased demand for products, as customers highly value transparency and reliability when making food choices. Second, the study provides valuable insights for restaurant managers considering the blockchain implementation as a strategic tool to attract and retain customers. The security and immutability of blockchain enhance traceability and trustworthiness, enabling restaurants to offer transparent information about their food products (Queiroz et al., 2019; Duan et al., 2020). By providing this transparency, restaurants can elevate customers' perceptions of food products and strengthen their trust in the establishment. Third, encouraging blockchain adoption in the F&B industry empowers government regulators to enhance food safety and quality standards, leading to improved public health outcomes and reduced economic costs related to foodborne illnesses. This involves establishing regulatory frameworks, promoting industry collaboration, and investing in necessary infrastructure. Actions include collaborating with experts and organizations to establish standardized practices and guidelines for blockchain implementation, addressing concerns regarding cost, scalability, and interoperability to facilitate adoption, and facilitating knowledge-sharing platforms and workshops to educate industry professionals about the benefits and practical applications of blockchain in the F&B industry. Engaging in public- private partnerships to invest in research and development is also crucial for streamlining blockchain implementation and addressing technological or operational challenges. Fourth, the adoption of blockchain empowers customers by providing them with reliable and trustworthy information about the safety, quality, and naturalness of their food. This empowers them to make more informed decisions about their food choices, leading to improved health outcomes and increased confidence in the food they consume. Educating consumers through consumer education initiatives is crucial to ensure they understand the value of blockchain-enabled traceability. Fifth, collaboration between destination management operators and local restaurants can result in the development of promotional programs focused on blockchain adoption. These 21 activities can highlight the importance of traceability in the food supply chain, differentiating the destination from competitors and attracting visitors who prioritize information transparency about food products. 7.4 Limitations and future research This study has several limitations. Firstly, implementing a blockchain-based system requires a significant investment of time and finances. While a video demonstration was used to simulate the blockchain prototype, it may not provide a deep understanding of its technical aspects. Real-world usage could present challenges not evident in the demonstration, and the lack of hands-on experience with blockchain may limit the evaluation of practical considerations. Secondly, the acceptance and adoption of QR code menus by consumers should be considered as a potential limitation. Although the study highlights the benefits of using QR codes, it does not specifically address customer attitudes and preferences towards this technology. Varying consumer perceptions of QR codes may impact the feasibility and success of blockchain implementation in restaurant menus. Thirdly, this research primarily focuses on signaling theory to analyze how blockchain traceability influences customer food perceptions and the dining experience. column1: Blockchain technology in circular economy: Unpacking the potential issues and critical echoes through data triangulation and natural language processing
column2: This study aims to identify the current status, potential issues and critical echoes in the integration of blockchain within circular economy (CE) practices. This study utilizes multiple data sources and synthesizes 91 published articles, and over 11,182 social media documents. Word‐embedding‐based clustering technique is employed to derive topics and themes on the use of blockchain in CE. The result of the study demonstrates that industries seek to implement blockchain for CE practices to automate processes for higher efficiency. However, issues revolving around blockchain governance and ethics, the impact of global trade facilitation, the skills required to implement blockchain, and sustainable reverse logistics within CE practices are major concerns. Additionally, acheiving a good return on investment while using blockchain for CE practices is another factor of concern for decision‐makers. This is the first study of its kind to discover topics, themes, potential issues, and critical echoes of integrating blockchain in CE through data triangulation. The results of this study are relevant to managers and policymakers, providing insights into leveraging up‐to‐date developments to address challenges in integrating blockchain within CE practices.
column3:
This study used data triangulation and natural language processing to investigate how blockchain may be applied in CE practices. Four major themes that have received a lot of attention in the published literature and on social media have emerged from this analysis: “global trade facilitation in the CE,” “sustainable reverse logistics and waste reduction in the CE,” “blockchain governance and ethics in the CE,” and “resource recycling and optimization in the CE.” RQ1 served as the source for these themes. Following that, every subject was thoroughly investigated to understand the challenges, issues, and benefits related to the use of blockchain technology in CE and to tackle RQ2.The primary focus of the first theme, “Blockchain Governance and Ethics in the CE,” is how important blockchain governance is to the advancement of CE principles. In addition to solving issues with scalability, energy consumption, data privacy, and ethical considerations, it promotes confidence through transparency, traceability, and decentralization. Social media conversations focus a lot of emphasis on the second theme, which is “Global trade facilitation in the CE.” It highlights the significant advantages of incorporating blockchain technology for international commerce inside the CE, including reduced counterfeiting, transparency, provenance verification, and automated smart contracts—all of which improve sustainability. The third theme highlights blockchain substantial potential to advance sustainability in this field: “Sustainable reverse logistics and waste reduction in the CE.” It offers data-driven insights, automation, traceability, and transparency to address important supply chain management issues. The fourth theme, “Resource recycling and optimization in the CE,” emphasizes how blockchain technology significantly improves resource recycling and optimization in the CE. Transparency, security, and efficiency are the means by which this is accomplished.Utilizing social media data may have certain intrinsic limits due to its vulnerability to several influencing variables, including the ever-changing nature of social media trends, time and spatial constraints, and platform-introduced algorithmic biases. These external factors might cause data variations, which would affect the study's overall robustness and generalizability. Social media data's intrinsic lack of representativeness—which results from its propensity to be biased toward particular user groups or demographics—is another important restriction. Even while secondary databases provide useful information, it is best to collect data directly from a wide range of stakeholders, maybe via techniques like in-person interviews or other direct forms of communication. This method makes it easier to find more relevant topics and promotes a better understanding of the difficulties and problems associated with integrating blockchain technology into CE processes. Speaking with decision makers face-to-face gives researchers the chance to ask follow-up questions and get explanations on points that need more explanation. By ensuring that the data collected is accurate and pertinent, this iterative approach aligns the data with the goals of the research. Furthermore, direct interaction between researchers and practitioners builds trust and connections that serve as a solid foundation for future cooperation and information sharing.In this study, we discerned themes that encapsulate the perspectives of various stakeholders in use of blockchain for CE practices. This insight was achieved through the application of data triangulation and natural language processing. As these themes are inherently interconnected, it is worth noting that, for instance, “sustainable reverse logistics and waste reduction in the CE” and “resource recycling and optimization in the CE” are closely intertwined within the framework of the CE. These themes collaborate to promote sustainability, waste minimization, and resource optimization, simultaneously contributing to environmental and economic objectives. Also to establish concrete linkages among these themes, researchers may employ them as the foundational framework for constructing a relational model. This model can subsequently undergo empirical validation through various methodologies. This prospective model, nurtured by emerging researchers, possesses the potential to provide invaluable insights and guidance to decision-makers aiming to make informed choices during the implementation of blockchain in CE practices. Furthermore, based on our findings we propose future research directions in Table 13 below:TABLE 13.
 Theme based future research avenues (Source: Authors' own work).ThemesFuture research directionsTheme 1: Blockchain governance and ethics in the CEOne of the central future research avenues is framing standardized frameworks for the use of blockchain in CE under ethical considerations. Also, future researchers may use ethics theory to examine the importance of ethical conduct in blockchain applications in CE.Theme 2: Global trade facilitation in CEFuture scholars may develop a framework to study how blockchain affects international trade including the global supply chain in the context of CE. Researchers might also investigate how smart contracts simplify international transactions and compliance. Here, future researchers can use transaction cost economics theory to examine global trade in CE.Theme 3: Sustainable reverse logistics and waste reduction in the CEA vital avenue for future research is to formulate a model that makes it easier to use blockchain in circular supply chains involving reverse logistics by maximizing product recycling and returns. Another important avenue for future researchers is to develop stakeholder collaboration models for blockchain-based reverse logistics optimization and validate them empirically. Use of supply chain practice-based view can be used to examine the sustainable reverse logistics practices in enhancing performance in supply chain networks.Theme 4: Resource recycling and optimization in the CEFuture researchers can focus on proposing a model for evaluating the role of blockchain in optimizing resource recycling processes and minimizing environmental impact. Another avenue for research is to investigate the potential for tokenization in incentivizing individuals and businesses to actively participate in recycling efforts. Future researchers can use operations research theories to examine the scope for resource recycling and optimization.The proposed avenues for future research act as a roadmap for future researchers as they delve deeper into and develop the topics that have been highlighted in relation to BT and CE.

column1: Dynamic spillovers between leading cryptocurrencies and derivatives tokens: Insights from a quantile VAR approach
column2: We investigate spillovers between leading cryptocurrencies and derivative tokens, a new asset class that facilitates derivative trading on blockchain platforms. Using data on the closing prices of two major cryptocurrencies (Bitcoin and Ethereum) and the 10 largest derivative tokens from December 2020 to February 2023, we find significant spillovers across the markets across all the quantiles, especially at the extreme quantiles or during stressed periods. Moreover, derivative tokens are more influenced by Ethereum than Bitcoin movements, with the behavior of derivative tokens varies across tokens. Results offer implications for investors and policymakers.
column3: 6 Conclusions Derivative tokens are a new class of decentralized financial assets, which provides investors with an alternative for gaining exposure to the derivative market. We examine spillovers between derivative tokens and major cryptocurrencies from December 2020 to February 2023 using a quantile connectedness approach. We find that derivative tokens are more connected to Ethereum than to Bitcoin across all the quantiles. In addition, connectedness between derivative tokens and major cryptocurrencies is significant across all quantiles, but especially at extreme upper and lower quantiles. Results also suggest that degrees of connectedness between derivative tokens and major cryptocurrencies vary across the tokens. For example, SXN and SRM are highly connected to Bitcoin and Ethereum, while other derivative tokens are less connected. Among the derivative tokens, SNX and SRM are also the largest net shock transmitters, and MIR and DDX are the largest net shock receivers. Overall, we document the time-varying nature of the spillovers across Bitcoin, Ethereum and the derivative token markets, where the connectedness among the markets tends to increase during stressed periods. Our findings have several implications. We show that derivative tokens are a separate asset class, with substantial differences among the behaviors of each token. Additionally, connectedness between derivative tokens and major cryptocurrencies increases at extreme quantiles and during stress periods. Altogether, results suggest that the diversification benefits of derivative tokens against Bitcoin or Ethereum risks vary across the tokens and market conditions. For investors, our results imply opportunities for hedging Bitcoin with derivative tokens, while the hedging benefits of derivative tokens against Ethereum are more limited. Further, derivative token investors focus on movements in Ethereum rather than Bitcoin, given the larger influence of Ethereum on derivative tokens. Overall, as derivative tokens are linked to many other underlying assets such as stocks, bonds, commodities, currencies, it is crucial that investors analyze them carefully before incorporating them into their portfolio. Specifically, as the price of derivative tokens is derived from fluctuations in the underlying assets, their hedging performance depends on the behavior of the underlying assets. Our results also highlight the importance of understanding the algorithm behind each derivative token, as tokens derived from similar algorithms (Proof-of-Stake, Proof-of-Work) tend to be highly connected to one another. Policymakers can take advantage of our results to identify the derivative tokens that offer the least contagion risks toward other cryptocurrencies. Our results also highlight the relevance of monitoring the cryptocurrency market during a market downturn. As the DeFi market continues to expand, doing this contributes to the stability of the overall financial systems. Finally, regulatory changes to mitigate the effects of extreme events such as cryptocurrency bankruptcies or exchange collapses will lower the contagion between derivative tokens and conventional cryptocurrency markets. This will improve the diversification benefits of derivative tokens, thereby increasing their role as an additional risk mitigation tool. Our paper provides several directions for future research. For example, studying the hedging and safe-haven properties of derivative tokens compared to other assets such as conventional derivatives, conventional cryptocurrencies and precious metals is relevant for investors to design effective diversification strategies. Future research could also explore the tail risk spillovers across derivative tokens, particularly in response to negative shocks such as the recent bank collapses and the collapse of FTX. An analysis of the determinants of spillovers across derivative tokens could provide important insights for investors and policymakers. Finally, an investigation of the effect of blockchain regulations can improve the understanding of the market for derivative tokens.

column1: Exploring the potential of blockchain-enabled smart contracts for achieving net-zero emissions: An empirical study
column2: A sustainable future entails addressing net‐zero emissions, which balances greenhouse gas emissions, thereby mitigating climate change. This study explores the relationship between the information quality, system quality, and service quality of blockchain‐enabled smart contracts (BSCs) with collaboration quality to achieve net‐zero emissions. The study further explores the role of collaboration quality in influencing the intention‐to‐use BSC and organizational satisfaction. The study employed the revised DeLone and McLean model and validated it with data from 434 respondents using structural equation modeling. The results validate all the hypotheses derived from the updated DeLone and McLean information system (IS) success model. There exist significant relationships between information quality, system quality, and service quality in the BSCs leading to collaboration quality to achieve net‐zero emissions. The study establishes the significant role of collaboration quality which positively impacts usage behavior and organizational satisfaction, mediated by the intention to use. The findings of this study offer insights for organizations and policymakers seeking to harness blockchain for environmental sustainability.
column3: The primary objective of this study was to analyze the relationships between IQ, SQ, and SEQ in BSCs and their impact on CQ. Additionally, the research examined how CQ influences the IU BSC and OS with the use of BSCs to promote net-zero emissions. The study used updated DeLone and McLean model to highlight the relationship between IQ, SQ, and SEQ in BSC and their impact on CQ. The research analyzed the significance of CQ in promoting IU that leads to OS. The results supported all seven hypotheses. The study highlights the significance of IQ, SEQ, and SQ in promoting sharing among various stakeholders leading to CQ. Further, efficient collaboration leads to intent of use. Thus, the study highlights the usage of BSC enhances CQ leading to uptake of the solution. Also IU leads to organization satisfaction. This suggests that an efficient and collaborative blockchain-enabled smart-contract system raises user intention, while simultaneously enhancing OS. Because of this, the study's importance rests in its ability to guide businesses' practical applications and academic research toward more efficient and cooperative ways of employing BSCs to reach net-zero emissions.The limitations of this study involve its use of cross-sectional data. However, we have taken care to control and minimize the risk of method bias in this study. Future studies could consider the use of panel data to test the model. While BSCs offer exciting possibilities for achieving net-zero emissions, it is essential to address these limitations and challenges for successful and sustainable implementation. Collaboration among stakeholders, ongoing research, and adaptability to evolving technologies and regulations will be key to overcoming these obstacles. Future researchers could also study the adoption of BSCs from a behavioral perspective to ensure sustainability, examining what drives people and organizations to use BSCs in pursuit of net-zero emissions, including user motivation, trust, and perceived barriers.Further investigations into quantum-enhanced security measures within BSC frameworks, quantum-based scalability solutions, quantum machine learning for predictive analysis, quantum-inspired optimization for sustainable implementation, integration of quantum-enabled consensus mechanisms, behavioral aspects of BSC adoption using quantum decision-making models, and longitudinal studies with quantum-enhanced blockchain systems to track sustainability measures are some of the areas of future research at the intersection of quantum computing and BSCs for sustainability that warrant attention. In order to improve security, scalability, predictive analysis, optimization, consensus mechanisms, behavioral understanding, and longitudinal tracking within BSCs, this research could be extended to take advantage of quantum computing's capabilities. This will advance sustainable solutions toward achieving net-zero emissions and addressing current environmental concerns.

column1: Energy supply chain efficiency in the digital era: Evidence from China's listed companies
column2: With the widespread adoption of cutting-edge digital technologies, including big data, blockchain, artificial intelligence (AI), and cloud computing, the development and digitalization of the supply chain are experiencing significant integration. According to China's Fourteenth Five-Year Plan for a Modern Energy System, the country has embarked on a new phase of constructing a modern energy system. An accelerating trend in the digital upgrading of energy businesses marks a period of innovation and upgrading for the modern energy industry. Although policy documents highlight the role of digital technology in advancing the digital transformation of energy businesses, the underlying relationships and transmission mechanisms have yet to be fully explored, underscoring the necessity for targeted policy development. This study examines the link between enterprise digital transformation and energy supply chain efficiency, utilizing a bidirectional fixed-effects framework and analyzing data from 112 listed companies in the energy sector from 2011 to 2019. Employing a three-stage DEA model and text analysis to measure the primary indicators, findings suggest that digital transformation enhances energy supply chain efficiency by fostering technological innovation, leveraging government subsidies, and increasing openness levels. Moreover, the positive impact is more pronounced in large and private enterprises, especially in the eastern and northeastern regions. This study offers empirical support for the policy framework mentioned, advocating for the advancement of business digital transformation, the establishment and enhancement of digital supply chain systems, and the integration of supply chain enterprise resources upstream and downstream.
column3: 7 Conclusions and policy recommendations Currently, enterprises operate in a rapidly changing environment marked by significant advancements in data processing capabilities, ushering human society into a new era with a focus on digital elements. In this era of digital economic advancement, businesses are embracing digital modernization to deeply integrate supply chains with the digital economy. This integration is pivotal for establishing robust digital supply chain systems. Using information from 112 publicly traded companies in China from 2011 to 2019, this study investigates the impact of enterprise digital transformation on the efficiency of energy supply chains, analyzing foundational processes through theoretical frameworks and practical viewpoints. The baseline regression findings suggest that digital modernization significantly improves supply chain efficiency. Heterogeneity analysis shows this effect is particularly pronounced in large and private enterprises. Robustness tests confirm that the initial regression outcomes remain significant after adjusting sample sizes, expanding control variables, and changing measurement methods, underscoring that digital transformation consistently enhances energy supply chain efficiency. Further analysis of intermediary mechanisms indicates that digital transformation primarily boosts efficiency by enhancing technological innovation, introducing government subsidies, and increasing openness. The results have significant policy implications for accelerating digital transition efforts at the enterprise level. On one front, advancing the digital modernization of energy businesses is crucial, leveraging digital technology in production and operations. This involves establishing user-centric supply chain management principles and using digital tools in the digitalization process. Actively engaging supply chain entities in procurement, R&D, production, sales, and service can strengthen market demand and drive digital adoption from both supply and demand sides. Integrating diverse digital technologies in the transformation process is essential. By emphasizing the role of data in supply chain operations, we can align data elements with supply chain components seamlessly. On another front, boosting investment in energy enterprises' exploration and creation efforts, expanding government subsidies, and fostering technological innovation are key. Using digital technology to streamline assets in energy supply chains facilitates efficient resource exchange, reduces information asymmetry, fosters trust, and enhances resource allocation efficiency. While large and private firms have advantages in digital transformation, promoting digitalization among small and mid-sized businesses is also necessary. Technological development can deepen digital technology integration into the economy, fostering collaborative innovation, promoting digital technology diffusion, reducing reliance on labor and capital, establishing independent information platforms, protecting innovation patents, refining management strategies, and reducing production costs. These actions enhance technical efficiency, facilitate resource consolidation, and pave the way for economies of scale. Allocating resources for government subsidies to support R&D projects will help energy enterprises accelerate digital transformation and enhance global competitiveness. Finally, fostering openness towards international markets can facilitate technology transfer, knowledge exchange, and stimulate innovation by exposing domestic firms to diverse perspectives and novel problem-solving approaches. To promote energy supply chain efficiency through corporate digital transformation, governments should prioritize technological innovation, offer subsidies, and encourage global engagement. Incentives for R&D, creating tech innovation hubs, and nurturing digital skills are crucial. Providing financial aid, reducing operational costs, and enacting supportive policies can drive digital investments. Engaging in global partnerships, liberalizing market access to attract foreign expertise, and participating in international standards setting can spur technological advancements and sustainable growth. The limitation of this paper lies in the exploration of how corporate digital transformation impacts the efficiency of the energy supply chain. Perhaps further in-depth research and discussion could be conducted from the internal perspective of enterprises, such as reducing default risk, improving information transparency, and enhancing transaction efficiency. This approach could provide guidance on how the government should direct enterprises while also informing businesses on how to improve their internal management and operational efficiency through digital transformation. In doing so, enterprises could attract government investments, creating a virtuous cycle.

column1: Blockchain adoption in retail operations: Stablecoins and traceability
column2: Retailers are embracing cryptocurrency payments to gain a competitive edge. However, the high volatility of traditional cryptocurrencies, such as Bitcoin, deters risk-averse consumers from using them regularly. This issue is particularly salient in retail markets with high product return rates, as consumers may bear the volatility risk by directly holding cryptocurrencies after claiming a refund. In real-world operations, collateralized stablecoins are proposed as a solution for transaction settlements, yet they still exhibit short-term volatility, as shown by empirical evidence. In this context, retailers can reduce the likelihood of returns by leveraging blockchain traceability to disclose information. This study analytically investigates how the retailer effectively utilizes the two blockchain functions to enhance firm profitability and increase consumer surplus. Our analysis shows that the retailer may offer a stingy or generous refund policy with blockchain adoption, depending on the degrees of information disclosure and price volatility. Next, we find that blockchain adoption always benefits consumers, though it may decrease social welfare. Interestingly, the benefit brought by blockchain to consumers declines if information is oversupplied. Further, we discover that blockchain adoption is likely to increase retailer profit when the information disclosure level is polarized (i.e., very high or low). Finally, the analysis reveals that greater stability of stablecoins benefits the retailer but hurts consumers. The reason for this seemingly counterintuitive result is that having stablecoins with better stability allows the retailer to charge a high price.
column3: 6 Conclusion Retailers endeavor to boost sales by utilizing the blockchain technology. This paper examines the unique impact of blockchain adoption on retail businesses from the perspective of the flows of information and finance. On one hand, cryptocurrency payments (esp., stablecoins) underpinned by blockchain offer advantages over traditional payment tools like credit cards. However, it creates disutility associated with cryptocurrency price volatility for consumers who may decide to return the product ex-post due to the uncertain product valuations. On the other hand, blockchain-enabled traceability discloses product valuations, thereby reducing consumer returns. This paper has shed light on the impact of the combined utilization of these two blockchain functions. Table 4 summarizes the welfare implications after blockchain is introduced. The bright side of blockchain adoption we derived is that it can achieve a win-win outcome for the retailer and consumers. In broad strokes, blockchain adoption brings payment facilitation and salvageability improvement to retailers. It also gives consumers the ability to obtain information in advance. We further concretize the role of blockchain adoption from perspectives of information disclosure level and price volatility of stablecoins. We find that blockchain adoption benefits the retailer when the information disclosure level is polarized. Otherwise, it may undermine the retailer because massive low-valuation consumers leave the market directly and the surplus of high-valuation consumers is not well exploited. Moreover, our result suggests that demanding a higher level of information disclosure is not necessarily beneficial for consumers because the marginal benefit can be offset by the higher price. In terms of the price volatility of stablecoins, we first find that a higher value for the volatility discount (i.e., either a lower degree of consumers’ risk aversion or a higher degree of stability of stablecoins) increases the retailer’s profit. By contrast, it reduces the total consumer surplus. This result is contrary to the conventional wisdom that the stability of cryptocurrencies protects consumer welfare. Several extended models are studied to establish more insights. First, we study the case that the retailer provides a flexible payment policy for consumers when blockchain is adopted. We interestingly find that blockchain adoption may reduce consumer surplus under the proposed flexible payment policy. Second, we discuss the impact of the mandatory full refund policy on blockchain-facilitated retail businesses. We find that the mandatory full refund policy may result in a lose-lose situation for consumers and the retailer. Third, we find that a higher degree of stability of stablecoins benefits consumers when the retailer is highly risk-averse relative to consumers. Fourth, we confirm the robustness of our key findings when the information disclosure level (or equivalently, the fraction of searchers) is endogenized. Finally, we incorporate consumers’ uncertainty about product mismatches. The result shows that blockchain is more valuable for the retailer and consumers in the market where product mismatches are more prevalent. We acknowledge that several assumptions have been made for analytical tractability or to prevent distractions from the focal points. First, we do not capture the case that cryptocurrencies are extremely volatile. Risk-seeking behavior is more relevant in this case. Second, relaxing the assumption on deterministic demand will likely yield new insights (see Teunter, Babai, Bokhorst, & Syntetos, 2018 for a good example). Third, it would be desirable to study retailers’ blockchain adoption strategies in a competitive environment ( Jiang, Li, Wang, & Zhao, 2022; Zhang, Ren, Lan, & Yang, 2022 ). Finally, We expect future research to extend this study in the presence of secondary markets ( Lei, Liu, & Shum, 2022; Li, Feng, Govindan, & Xu, 2019 ).

column1: Blockchain enabled dynamic trust management method for the internet of medical things
column2: The Internet of Things (IoT) connects heterogeneous sensing devices with servers under the support of the network to monitor intelligent communication and real-time data transmission. The system caters well to the needs of medical services and also provides convenience for telemedicine. Many IoT-based solutions have been proposed for medical application scenarios. However, the unpredictable nature of communication links and device failures may lead to challenges in setting effective security policies for controlling these devices. Trust management has emerged as an ideal solution that can implement a dynamic management approach and regulate node connection requests. While centralized architectures require only a central node and relatively few devices, they are not suitable for large-scale medical facilities. In contrast, decentralized approaches based on blockchain technology have recently emerged as feasible solutions for IoT practices. Nevertheless, these decentralized approaches are vulnerable to potential attacks such as defaming honest nodes or improving the trust degrees of malicious nodes, which can compromise trust degrees within the system. This paper designs a blockchain-enabled trust management method for medical services based on the IoT, aiming to prevent malicious nodes from sending false trust levels. The proposed trust assessment model utilizes referees' direct experience and indirect feedback to recommend trustworthy medical services. The presented model provides a certain level of security against various types of attacks including malicious attacks, benevolent attacks, and on-off attacks. Experimental results illustrate that the model is robust and effective.
column3: 8 Conclusion Trust management in the IoMT is challenging due to the fragmentation of the IoT itself and the variety and complexity of devices. The IoMT aims to provide a secure transaction platform between smart medical devices. In the context of the IoMT, trust and reliability are used as the basis for trust evaluation, and trust can describe the service quality of the target nodes. In this paper, we propose a decentralized trust management method. Our method is fully decentralized and accounts for the social relationships between participants to guide trust rules. However, the scalability of the method is improved by using dynamic parameters such as the attenuation factor. The simulation results illustrate that our method has significant advantages in trust evaluation. Finding the best path with the lowest cost and most effective weighted combination will be challenging under the limitations of IoT devices, especially in the healthcare domain. Therefore, in future work, we will try to further optimize the trust feedback algorithm to increase the sensitivity of the model to malicious nodes and to correctly handle the recommendation errors of normal nodes.

column1: Can blockchain technologies enhance environmental sustainable development goals performance in manufacturing firms? Potential mediation of green supply chain management practices
column2: The nexus between manufacturing firms and the green environment is unavoidable. It is merely due to the huge waste generation and greenhouse gas emissions resulting from large‐scale production and complex supply chain management processes involved in manufacturing firms. Continuation of the traditional business practices during Industry 4.0 made it impossible for the manufacturing firm to commit to green environmental practices and comply with environmental SDGs. At odd, it requires novel business strategies to ensure compliance of manufacturing firms with environmental sustainable development goals (SDGs). Blockchain is an ideal technology for delivering green environmental‐related information because it offers real‐time, shareable, and entirely transparent data kept on an immutable ledger that is accessible to members of a network. These green environmental‐related information received in real‐time through blockchain technology help in the transformation of the traditional supply chain management practices into a more green supply chain management practice. This green transformation ensures business compliance with environmental SDGs and that compliance is shared with multiple stakeholders through blockchain technology in real‐time, thus approving a positive mediating role of green supply chain management practices between blockchain technology and environmental SDGs performance. The proposed strategic framework through various propositions development will mainly offer policy insights toward (a) identifying novel antecedents of blockchain technology, (b) offering insights toward upgrading the traditional supply chain management framework into a green supply chain management framework, and (c) illuminating novel mediating role of green supply chain management practices between blockchain technology and environmental SDGs performance.
column3: This study primarily aimed at examining the nexus between BCT and environmental SDGs performance mediated through GSCMPs. In line with that in the first place, this study explored five novel first-order antecedents of BCT, namely, technological consideration, organizational consideration, environmental consideration, individual consideration, and task consideration and 15 second-order antecedents of BCT (refer to Figure 4). These proposed antecedents will insight policymakers regarding the adoption of BCT. Blockchain is an ideal technology for receiving and delivering green environmental-related information to various stakeholders because it offers real-time, shareable, and entirely transparent data kept on an immutable ledger that is accessible to members of a network. These green environmental-related information received in real-time through BCT will persuade managers to comply with green practices in their supply chain. It is because various stakeholders nowadays demand manufacturing firms to ensure green practices during their production and supply chain process. This will eventually help in the transformation of the traditional SCM process into a more GSCMP. Secondly, in line with the potential mediating role of GSCMP, this study offers substitute variables for upgrading the traditional SCM process toward a GSCMP (refer to Figure 5). It is anticipated that the green upgradation of the traditional SCM process in the manufacturing firm will ensure compliance of manufacturing firms with environmental SDGs that is (06: clean water and sanitation) (07: affordable and clean energy), (13:climate action), (14: life below water) and (15: life on land). Thus it approves the positive mediating role of GSCMp. This study offers various implications for managers and methods.5.1 Managerial implicationThis study offers insights into management in manufacturing firms in three ways. First, it guides them about the novel antecedents of BCT. Holistically, it will guide management in selecting secure and complex technology that has superior benefits toward adopting BCT. Second, it illuminates management about the readiness level of their organization toward the adoption of BCT. In small organizations, a superior role from the top management is required in the adoption of BCT. In the third place, this study guides the management regarding the external environmental requirements for the adoption of BCT. It enriches the management in understanding the market dynamics of blockchain adoption and the available regulatory and government support for it. If the regulations and government support for the adoption of BCT are favorable, then the management must strategise toward its adoption. In the fourth place, in terms of individual consideration, this study guides the management to examine privacy before the adoption of the new BCT for better trust and positive expectations from the new blockchain system. Fifth, it guides the management on the total cost required for adopting the blockchain system and further guides them on whether the management would need to change existing business standards for it or not. It further illuminates the management on how to upgrade the traditional SCM process into a more green supply chain managing system toward achieving better compliance with environmental SDGs (refer to Figure 5).5.2 Methodological implicationThis study offers various methodological insights. In the first place, it offers novel five first-order and 15 second-order antecedents toward the adoption of BCT. It will serve as the methodological base for future studies to construct new scales for the data collection on BCT. The second methodological contribution this study offers is the provision of a substitute variable for transforming the traditional SCM process into a GSCMP. It will assist future researchers in data collection on GSCMP while examining environmental SDGs performance in manufacturing firms. Thirdly, and most importantly, this study offers logical integration of various variables toward improving environmental SDGs performance. In line with that, it offers a novel mediating role of the green supply chian management practices between the nexus of blockchian adoption and environmental SDG performance.5.3 Future researchFor future work, this study anticipates collecting data on the proposed framework by using the content analysis technique. It will statistically affirm the validity of this proposed model and will lead to the generation of a novel scale on the nexus between BCT and environmental SDGs mediated by GSCMPs.

column1: Enhancing Digital Advertising with Blockchain Technology
column2: The increasing popularity of blockchain technology (BCT) has spurred interest in its potential to rejuvenate the digital advertising ecosystem. Due to its transparency, decentralization, and immutability, BCT offers the potential for customer-oriented, secure, and open platforms that might improve interactions between consumers and businesses. This article investigates applications of BCT in digital advertising and develops an integrative framework to classify innovations at this intersection. With a systematic literature review and Delphi study, the authors examine ten relevant use cases and compile qualitative and quantitative data on the expected probability of realization, expected impact on the industry, desirability of occurrence, and market establishment duration. The results reveal organizational activity theory–informed areas of innovation and provide useful insights for managers, researchers, and policy makers. Managers should focus on contextual innovations such as rewarding web users for web interactions, rewarding content creators for their contributions, and ensuring user data security as the most relevant potential applications. Boundary innovations require a better understanding before deploying solutions aimed at increasing advertising supply chain transparency, mitigating fraud, and verifying content. For domain-based innovation areas, researchers must rethink their foundations. Finally, the authors propose a detailed research agenda.
column3: Although the number of BCT applications in marketing, and specifically ABA, are increasing (Stallone, Wetzels, and Klaas 2021), the technology has been changing and manifesting different generational developments in application areas, in consensus models, in the utility of smart contracts, in energy and cost requirements, and in execution speed and scalability (Mukherjee and Pradhan 2021). Academia must consider these dynamics to stay relevant with respect to research methodologies and results in the field of BCT.The current article contributes to bodies of knowledge in adtech, BCT, and OAT. Our literature review identifies 34 publications that touch on important ABA issues by proposing an integrative, comprehensible, and flexible framework and investigating applications and research questions. These publications yield ten ABA use cases: digital advertising transparency, user data security, rewarding web users, ad fraud mitigation, rewarding content creators, content verification, mobile advertising, social advertising, affiliate advertising, and search engine advertising. Our research represents the first empirical identification of ABA. We bounce them off our framework synthesizing ABA into three areas of innovation: domain, boundary, and context. To gather in-depth, long-term insights from these use cases, we applied a two-round Delphi methodology. The results delineate the expected probability of realization, expected impact on the advertising industry, desirability within the industry, and expected market establishment duration, with clear differences among the three innovation areas: Our research leads us to believe that use cases in the field of contextual innovations (rewarding content creators, user data security, and rewarding web users) will have the greatest impact on the industry and the highest expected probability of realization, though our panelists were least confident about the innovation area when assessing the expected probability of realization and market establishment duration. Thus, we propose research questions, including methodologies, to increase confidence in the use cases.The limitations of this study provide opportunities for further research. We followed established practices to select our group of experts, but the results might be influenced by their biases (e.g., projection, belief, availability, confirmation, anthropic bias) (Valerdi 2011). Our research focuses on conceptual aspects of the development of the DAE and only touches on other aspects, such as regulation. Although providing a useful framework for understanding not only the DAE, but the ABA within, our results may oversimplify the complex nature of the system. We therefore expect scholars to challenge our findings and continue our integration processes with new, emerging innovations in ABA into the areas we have identified and discussed.As Scott Galloway (2022) notes, “Scarcity and authenticity are powerful, and not always forces for good.… Amidst the scams and bubbles, credible scarcity and authenticity will unlock real value in digital markets.”

column1: The nexus of supply chain performance and blockchain technology in the digitalization era: Insights from a fast-growing economy
column2: This article extends the coverage of previous studies and addresses persistent gaps in the literature by assessing the simultaneous effects of adopting blockchain technology (BCT) on supply chain performance. It empirically examines the indirect effect of BCT adoption on supply chain performance through the mediating variables of supply chain agility, adaptability, transparency and coordination, based on the expanded triple A supply chain concept. The study analyzes data from manufacturing firms listed on the Indonesian Stock Exchange. The findings align with propositions derived from the Resource Based View (RBV), in which capabilities viewed as mediators—rather than testing for direct effects of BCT on organizational performance—are the most likely scenario for multifaceted supply chain operations. This study contributes to the ongoing debate on the relationship between BCT and organizational performance. The research offers insights for policymakers and blockchain vendors into this relationship.
column3: 7 Conclusions, limitations and future research directions This study aimed to empirically test the indirect effects of the adoption of BCT on supply chain performance through various supply chain capabilities, which are part of the resources that provide firms with competitive advantage. Specifically, we investigated the influence of BCT adoption on supply chain performance via the agility, adaptability, alignment/coordination and transparency of the supply chain, an extension of the triple A supply chain aspects. While a growing body of literature in the field of SCM highlights the significant role of BCT in enhancing various aspects of the supply chain ( Kshetri, 2018; Lim et al., 2021; Pan et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2021; Wang, Singgih, et al., 2019 ), there is a gap in the prior research regarding these relationships. The findings of this study indicate that the adoption of BCT can indirectly enhance supply chain performance through improvements in agility, adaptability, transparency, and coordination. Finally, the concept of the triple A SCM capabilities could leverage the functionalities offered by BCT, resulting in unique competencies for supply chains. 7.1 Limitations As with all research, this study does possess certain limitations. First, the impact of firm size was not taken into account, which could potentially influence the relationships between variables. It is possible that different-sized firms may experience different effects when adopting BCT in the supply chain. Second, the generalizability of our findings to other countries may be limited. While previous research by Fosso Wamba et al. (2020) and Queiroz and Fosso Wamba (2019) suggests that there are no significant differences in BCT adoption between countries (such as India and the US), it is important to recognize that BCT acceptance is not yet uniform globally. The advantages, limitations, and regulatory frameworks surrounding BCT implementation can vary across different countries, leading to diverse perceptions and adoption patterns. Finally, this study solely focuses on the performance of the supply chain and does not consider other dimensions of performance, such as financial or operational performance.

column1: Money, Bitcoin, and Monetary Policy
column2: Abstract A search‐theoretic model is constructed, where money and Bitcoin can be used as mediums of exchange. We investigate how each currency facilitates transactions and how they compete with each other. Quantitative analysis shows that welfare in an economy with both money and Bitcoin is lower than in a money‐only economy due to congestions in the confirmation of Bitcoin transactions and that the welfare gap between the two economies expands as inflation rises. Moreover, an increase in transaction fees for Bitcoin can increase welfare by reducing inefficient Bitcoin transactions.
column3: In this paper, we study how the central bank-issued money and a cryptocurrency (Bitcoin) compete as an MOE, and how monetary policy and one of the main features of the current Bitcoin system (i.e., transaction fees) affect economic activities and welfare. Our quantitative analysis demonstrates that Bitcoin can compete meaningfully with money only when the inflation rate is sufficiently high, considering the current Bitcoin system. Strikingly, economic welfare in the money-only economy is higher than that in the coexistence economy. The lower welfare in the coexistence economy is primarily attributed to delayed settlements in the current Bitcoin system.The welfare gap between the coexistence economy and the money-only economy increases in inflation. Specifically, as the inflation rate increases, money is substituted for Bitcoin, which increases Bitcoin transactions. An increase in Bitcoin transactions raises the time for validation and recording Bitcoin transactions due to the restriction on the number of transactions that each block can contain. This, in turn, aggravates the delivery lags of goods when Bitcoin is used as an MOE. Thus, effective consumption and welfare decrease further in the coexistence economy.In addition, welfare increases in the transaction fee rate in the coexistence economy because an increase in the transaction fee rate leads to an increase in money transactions, which is more efficient as an MOE, and a decrease in Bitcoin transactions. A decrease in Bitcoin transactions also improves the efficiency of Bitcoin. On the other hand, in the Bitcoin-only economy, economic welfare can be maximized by minimizing the transaction fees that reduce the trade volume.

column1: Optimizing the Nonfungible Token Ecosystem: Effects of Business Models, Secondary Markets, and Royalties
column2: The adoption of blockchain technology has spurred significant growth in the global Non-fungible tokens (NFT) market, which distinguishes itself from traditional markets by features such as free second-hand transactions and creator royalties. To navigate this burgeoning landscape, diverse business models have emerged, such as No secondary market and no royalties, Secondary market but no royalties, and Secondary market with royalties (mandatory royalty). In response, our theoretical model delves into the impact of these models on creator decisions, profits, consumer surplus, and social welfare. The NFT secondary market proves pivotal, enabling creators to set higher prices and enhance profits. Interestingly, introducing a creator royalty, under certain conditions, further boosts profits. Contrary to expectations, a low royalty doesn't always harm consumers; in fact, a sufficiently high royalty prompts creators to lower regular selling prices, fostering secondary transactions and expanding consumer surplus. Beyond the secondary market's conventional role in improving social welfare, our research reveals that a well-calibrated royalty, coupled with creator investment in NFT quality, can amplify social welfare. A low royalty incentivizes creators to prioritize highquality NFT production. We also scrutinize mandatory versus optional royalty policies (Consumer Optional Royalty), finding that the creator's profit is higher under the optional royalty framework with moderate or substantial royalties. We recommend that NFT creators opt for a medium royalty rate when given the choice to set it themselves. Otherwise, in instances where the royalty rate is predetermined, creators are better with mandatory (optional) royalty when royalty is small (large).
column3: Motivated by the burgeoning NFT market, this study metic- ulously examines three prevalent NFT business models no secondary market and no royalties, secondary market but no royalties, and secondary market with royalties and introduces a novel model, consumer optional royalties. Our analysis com- prehensively explores the implications of each business model on NFT creators, consumers, and societal dynamics. In the initial analysis, the scarcity of NFT products empowers creators to command higher prices and accrue greater profits through the introduction of an NFT second-hand market. In addition, the second-hand market serves as a powerful incentive for creators to elevate product quality, especially when NFT quality is endogenous. This enhancement in product quality not only augments CS but also contributes to societal welfare by expanding NFT accessibility. Furthermore, our findings reveal that NFT creators can op- timize profits from royalties only when the royalty is low. Conversely, under a high royalty scenario, consumer reluctance to resell NFTs prompts creators to lower selling prices, thereby stimulating secondary transactions but diminishing profit mar- gins. Notably, a substantial royalty enhances CS by bolstering the retention of NFTs by first-period consumers in the second period, countering losses incurred by consumers engaged in secondary transactions. From a social welfare perspective, we recommend that regu- lators carefully consider the implications of allowing nonpro- fessional NFT creators to collect creator fees. The potential benefits of royalties to creators or consumers may not sufficiently outweigh the losses incurred by the other party when royalty rates are either too low or too high. In contrast, for professional creators, regulatory encouragement for creator fees is advised, contingent upon maintaining a low royalty. A diminished royalty stimulates creators to enhance NFT quality, fostering a mutually beneficial scenario for both creators and consumers. Therefore, when the royalty ratio is small, nonprofessional creators are suggested to learn and master relevant professional background knowledge to improve the quality of the NFTs. Finally, our study uncovers that, compared to mandatory royalties, consumer optional royalties outperform in terms of both creator benefits and social welfare when the royalty is not excessively small. This suggests that NFT creators should consider adopting optional royalties when faced with moderate or large royalties. When creators possess the autonomy to de- termine royalties, our findings reveal that the optimal royalty, as decided by professional creators under both royalty policies, yields the highest profit and societal welfare. Consequently, we advocate for regulatory frameworks that delegate royalty-setting authority to professional creators under mandatory royalties while restricting royalty collection rights for nonprofessional NFT creators. These results open promising avenues for further exploration. First, our model contemplates a monopoly NFT creator, while practical scenarios involve multiple NFT creators competing in the market. Second, investigating the decision-making processes of NFT trading platforms presents a compelling avenue for future research, given the pivotal role these platforms play in the majority of NFT transactions with the instrument of transaction charges. Third, it will be interesting to consider consumer returns or anticipated regret in the NFT market [36], [37].

column1: In Art We Trust
column2: Whereas trust is the cornerstone of any market’s functioning, it is of particular importance in markets that are unregulated, illiquid, and opaque, such as the art market. This study examines the role of authenticity, as captured by provenance information in auction catalogs, on the probability of auctioned oil paintings, watercolors, and prints being sold; their price formation; and returns. Auction catalogs include four authenticity dimensions: pedigree (ownership “blockchain,” descendance information; type of past owners, such as renowned collectors; and past sales records), exhibition history (e.g., in famous museums or galleries), literature coverage (e.g., in catalogues raisonnés or authoritative press), and certification (e.g., artist’s physical testimonial, expert opinions). We find that trust, proxied by provenance information, increases the probability of a work being sold by up to 4%, leads to hammer price premiums up to 54%, and increases annualized returns by 5%–16%. To address potential endogeneity problems between the provision of provenance and past prices/price expectations, we perform quasi-natural experiments in difference-in-differences settings on auction houses’ provenance policy changes following authenticity litigation and on a contamination effect of the discovery of fakes and forgeries on the oeuvre of forged artists. We also test transactions less affected by past prices, such as estate sales following the death of a collector. The findings on the relation between provenance and prices are robust to artist reputation, artistic style, auction house reputation, art market liquidity, and artist career timing. This paper was accepted by Tomasz Piskorski, finance. Funding: Yuexin Li gratefully acknowledges supports from the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grant 72204257] and the Area Studies Fund of Renmin University of China [Grant AS2022002]. This study is partially funded by the Tilburg Alumni Fund. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2022.4633 .
column3: Trust is key for any type of market but particularly forilliquid, opaque, and largely unregulated markets, suchas the art market. A lack of trust undermines sales andprices, which is worsened when fakes and forgeries arerumored to circulate in the art market. Therefore, guar-antees about the authenticity of an art object are pivotalin creating trust, and the provision of provenance can bea (partial) solution by emitting a signal about the art�sauthenticity. Provenance comprises records of owner-ship or pedigree, exhibition history, literature coverage,and certification, all of which relate to the artwork�sauthenticity and can enhance trustworthiness of theobject offered for sale.
