The current paper explores this effectiveness by building an analytical model involving four kinds of players: a multi-sided platform, a customer, a bank, and multiple transportation service providers. In this setting, a traditional SCF model with Platform Undertakes Guarantee (PUG) and a novel SCF strategy with self-guarantee (i.e. Customer Undertakes Guarantee (CUG)) are analysed. The results indicate that CUG can bring a Pareto improvement for the market compared to PUG. Although CUG displays higher efficiency, it is not always beneficial to the platform when the customer's opportunity cost rate is higher than the platform's. Furthermore, to mitigate credit risk caused by a low-credit customer, the platform may employ a prepayment strategy. Analytical results of this study indicate that the prepayment ratio does not affect the customer's cost, and thus, providing a high prepayment ratio but a relatively low service fee rate to low-credit customers is suggested to the platform.
column3: Blockchain technology helps firms use self-guarantee in traditional SCF, which inspires analysis of the effectiveness of self-guarantee in multi-sided markets. To examine this effectiveness, we establish a Stackelberg game consisting of a leading platform, a bank on the capital supply side, multiple transportation service providers on the logistics supply side and a customer on the capital and logistics demand side. Based on this game, we studied PUG with a guarantee by the platform and CUG with a guarantee by the customer himself in this paper. Our work focuses only on the situation that the actions of service providers are symmetric in bid auctions, but asymmetric situations could be examined in the future. Interesting future directions which should be explored are as follows. Firstly, the second price auction or English auction could be analysed based on our model, so the results with this type of auction can be compared with our research results to verify whether the first-price auction is still the best, in agreement with Tamura ( Citation 2016). Secondly, it would be interesting to extend this paper to consider the overall projects scenario where customers have different credit levels based on a certain distribution, which may bring new findings about credit levels. Thirdly, analysing the topic of supply-demand matching based on this work, the macro influencing factors such as guarantee proportion may play a role. Finally, subsidies in the transaction system could be considered. For example, the platform could promise to give a subsidy when the customer repays the principal and interest on time, which may further increase the system service level and promote the system coordination.

column1: InsurTech development: Evidence from Chinese media reports
column2: Abstract As a new trend, InsurTech is shaking up every link of the traditional insurance industry chain. Facilitated by many factors such as capital investment, new technology development and the high penetration rate of e-commerce, China has become an important market for the development of InsurTech. This paper uses text mining technology and Python to analyze the word frequency of 25,662 InsurTech-related news reports from 2015 to 2019 in China. It also applies the term frequency-inverse document frequency (TFIDF) indicator to test the trends and features of InsurTech's development in China. Both word frequency and TFIDF show that InsurTech's media reports primarily focus on “insurance”, “finance”, and “science and technology”; their rankings change annually. “Blockchain” is the key technology for different years. Data is getting more and more attention. The evidence provided in this article has implications for global technological innovation in insurance. To our best knowledge, this is the first large-scale Chinese media reports-based study to investigate the characteristics of the China InsurTech development.
column3: 5 Conclusion and inspiration This paper uses text mining technology and Python to analyze word frequency in 25,662 InsurTech-related news reports in China from 2015 to 2019 in order to identify the hotspots and development trends in the InsurTech industry. The results of the word frequency analysis show that “insurance”, “science and technology”, and “finance” are the core concepts of InsurTech, while “platform” and “innovation” comprise the main content. “Financing” and “investment” were hot topics in the industry in both 2015 and 2016, but their importance dropped from 2017 to 2019. New technologies such as “blockchain”, and “artificial intelligence” are becoming the new hotspots. The application of those technologies will be the industry's major research and development direction in the future. This study also uses the TFIDF method to filter out high-frequency but less meaningful words and counts the top 20 words from 2015 to 2019. The results show that the importance of “insurance”, “science & technology”, “finance”, and “investment” is similar to that in the word frequency statistics. “Platform” was the major content of InsurTech development in China, and “blockchain” has become its technology focus, which again confirms the results of the word frequency analysis. The ranking of the “data” in the word frequency list increased in 2019, indicating an increasing attention to the importance of data. There are many forces that drive the development of China InsurTech, such as government's policies, public media coverage, and the technology. The findings of our study have important implications for the development of the global InsurTech industry, which is still in the development stage. The application of most emerging technologies, and even the technologies themselves, are still in the research and development stage. Many technical difficulties must still be overcome, and their commercial viability has not yet been proven. InsurTech still has a long way to go before it reaches maturity. The media coverage hints at its rise and the shocks it could bring: it is expected to reshape the entire insurance ecosystem. Therefore, the rapid development of technologies calls for more public attention and requires more academic consideration and research.

column1: Blockchain technology in supply chain operations: Applications, challenges and research opportunities
column2: Highlights • Evaluate 178 research articles in the field of blockchain implementation in supply chains.• Identify the current trends of research on blockchain in different domains of supply chain operations.• Examine various supply chain functions that can be enhanced through blockchain technology.• Present strong excerpts of blockchain applications in supply chains across various industrial sectors.• Suggest managerial implications, highlight challenges and build a future research agenda.
column3: 8 Conclusion SCM has entered the big data era ( Choi et al., 2018; Kuo and Kusiak, 2019 ), and blockchain technology has emerged as a disruptive technology. It is commonly believed that blockchain has a huge potential to transform the SCs, both global and local, by improving operational efficiency, data management, responsiveness, transparency and smart contract management. With blockchain bursting out on the scene, it can act as a source of competitive advantage for companies, governments and all kinds of organization in the society. Investments are being made by different companies and countries in exploring the new applications with blockchain to achieve a higher operational efficiency. The blockchain industry is also moving toward various areas, including the standardization issue and the way to integrate different blockchain systems together. This article provides a thorough review of 178 research articles and covers several aspects of blockchain technology in SC and logistics management. It starts with a brief overview of blockchain architecture and its characteristics, as well as some of the important literature reviews on blockchain in SCs and the uniqueness of the current work. As mentioned earlier, the key benefits of blockchain in SCs, various applications of blockchain in different SC functions and operations, and societal impacts are some of the major aspects being covered in this review article, which are under-examined in the prior review papers. This work also adds values by summarizing the recent developments in blockchain and examining its potential applications in various sectors like healthcare, finance, technology, energy, agriculture, trade, government services, e-commerce, shipping, aviation and automotive sectors. The work has identified and covered all the pertinent research studies published in this field and will significantly help both academics and practitioners to have a better understanding of the related studies. Nevertheless, the managerial implications and related big theories for future developments of blockchain enabled SCs have been discussed. The societal impacts and various challenges associated with blockchain have been examined. All these could act as valuable references for researchers and supply chain managers. An extensive future research agenda in various SC functions and operations, business process management and SC sustainability including potential research in different industrial sectors has been proposed. Overall, this review article will help researchers and practitioners to better understand and identify SC areas and industry sectors in which blockchian technology could be used. The current trends, challenges, and potential scope for future research opportunities around the use of blockchain for supply chain operations are also discussed.

column1: What have we learnt from 10 years of fintech research? a scientometric analysis
column2: Abstract With the development of financial market and various demands of customers, the traditional financial industry begins to change the business process, risk controlling and business models. FinTech appears and develops rapidly in various business models to solve problems in the financial markets. This paper analyzes 629 FinTech business model papers in the Web of Science database. First, we analyze the overall growth trend, research area, research institutions and core authors in the Fintech business model based on the statistical analysis. Second, this paper builds the citation network of Fintech business model and analyzes citation clusters, the key nodes and pivot nodes and the dynamic evolution of co-cited keywords. Finally, we summarize the latest hot topics in the FinTech, which are mobile payment, microfinance, peer-to-peer lending platform and crowdfunding. In the future, the trend of the research is Blockchain and crowdfunding and they will have a subversive influence on the Fintech business model. The research ideas and conclusions in this paper are enlightening to the academic research the commercial practical application of Fintech.
column3: 5 Conclusion and further research FinTech business model has emerged as a research hotspot in recent years. Although a number of researchers have studied on the topic based on several sub-fields, there has been no research on the overall FinTech business model knowledge system. In particular, a quantitative analysis of the publication characteristics of a massive sample of FinTech business model publications and their citation frequencies has been lacking. Bibliometric research on FinTech business model enables us to obtain a firm understanding of the key research findings in the field using a scientific approach. The results of such research can inspire future research on FinTech and its application in the business world. In this paper, we applied bibliometrics to analyze FinTech business model-related research developments. Specifically, we described the overall trend of growth for FinTech business model publications, the areas of FinTech research, the most active research institutions and the core authors. In addition, we constructed co-citation clusters and analyzed hotspots of FinTech business model studies and their dynamic evolution. Based on our bibliometric analysis, we offer the following key conclusions: 1) FinTech business model is a field of study that has emerged in recent years. In 2007, there were only 14 citations. In 2017, this figure increased to 1013. The research excitement regarding FinTech business model in recent years is mainly due to the developments of Web communications technology, the computer storage and computation ability of big data. As we advance into the 21st century, new working formats for business processes, risk controls and business models have emerged in the traditional financial industry. To a large extent, traditional theories no longer apply. FinTech business model research has emerged in response to the pressing needs of the industry and the academic world and is now fast-growing. 2) Based on our empirical findings regarding citation networks, the latest FinTech business model research hotspots are mobile payment, micro-finance, P2P lending and crowdfunding. Since 2010, the popularity of smart phones and the improvement of mobile payment technology have provided the objective conditions for mobile payment, microfinance, P2P lending and crowdfunding are based on individual credit information and precise risk control. However, these factors cannot be effectively ascertained without the capture, storage and analysis of massive customer data. As technological facilities maturing, these emerging business models in the field of FinTech will gain additional attention. 3) This paper proposes Blockchain and crowdfunding research as the future trend of FinTech studies. To be specific, increasing number of researches focus on Blockchain-based application beyond Bitcoin, for example, smart cities, cryptocurrency systems ( Yli-Huumo et al., 2016 ; McConaghy et al., 2017 ; Lluïsa and Llacuna, 2018 ; Palmié et al., 2020 ). These studies indicate that Blockchain technology may have a disruptive impact on the financial industry. Besides, few researches can be found to analyze the influence of crowdfunding on the banking system, and existing research has not addressed the competition among crowdfunding platforms. Therefore, interesting research questions in this context can be identified: Are crowdfunding platforms competitors or complements to banks instead of substitutes? How do crowdfunding platforms compete? ( Gomber et al., 2017 ; Chen et al., 2019 ).
